67:22.ar: أَفَمَن يَمۡشِي مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦٓ أَهۡدَىٰٓ أَمَّن يَمۡشِي سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
67:22.en: Is he who goeth groping on his face more rightly guided, or he who walketh upright on a straight road

67:23.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنشَأَكُمۡ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَ وَٱلۡأَفۡـِٔدَةَۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَشۡكُرُونَ
67:23.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): He it is who gave you being, and hath assigned unto you ears and eyes and hearts. Small thanks give ye

67:24.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلَّذِي ذَرَأَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
67:24.en: Say: He it is Who multiplieth you in the earth, and unto Whom ye will be gathered

67:25.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلۡوَعۡدُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
67:25.en: And they say: When (will) this promise (be fulfilled), if ye are truthful

67:26.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡعِلۡمُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَإِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
67:26.en: Say: The knowledge is with Allah only, and I am but a plain warner

67:27.ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوۡهُ زُلۡفَةࣰ سِيٓـَٔتۡ وُجُوهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَقِيلَ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَدَّعُونَ
67:27.en: But when they see it nigh, the faces of those who disbelieve will be awry, and it will be said (unto them): This is that for which ye used to call

67:28.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَهۡلَكَنِيَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَن مَّعِيَ أَوۡ رَحِمَنَا فَمَن يُجِيرُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ مِنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
67:28.en: Say (O Muhammad): Have ye thought: Whether Allah causeth me (Muhammad) and those with me to perish or hath mercy on us, still, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful doom

67:29.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ وَعَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡنَاۖ فَسَتَعۡلَمُونَ مَنۡ هُوَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
67:29.en: Say: He is the Beneficent. In Him we believe and in Him we put our trust. And ye will soon know who it is that is in error manifest

67:30.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَصۡبَحَ مَآؤُكُمۡ غَوۡرࣰ ا فَمَن يَأۡتِيكُم بِمَآءࣲ مَّعِينِۭ
67:30.en: Say: Have ye thought: If (all) your water were to disappear into the earth, who then could bring you gushing water

67:1.ar: تَبَٰرَكَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
67:1.en: Blessed is He in Whose hand is the Sovereignty, and, He is Able to do all things

67:2.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلࣰ اۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
67:2.en: Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct; and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving

67:3.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ اۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتࣲۖ فَٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ هَلۡ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورࣲ‏
67:3.en: Who hath created seven heavens in harmony. Thou (Muhammad) canst see no fault in the Beneficent One's creation; then look again: Canst thou see any rifts

67:4.ar: ثُمَّ ٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيۡنِ يَنقَلِبۡ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَصَرُ خَاسِئࣰ ا وَهُوَ حَسِيرࣱ‏
67:4.en: Then look again and yet again, thy sight will return unto thee weakened and made dim

67:5.ar: وَلَقَدۡ زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهَا رُجُومࣰ ا لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِۖ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:5.en: And verily We have beautified the world's heaven with lamps, and We have made them missiles for the devils, and for them We have prepared the doom of flame

67:6.ar: وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
67:6.en: And for those who disbelieve in their Lord there is the doom of hell, a hapless journey's end

67:7.ar: إِذَآ أُلۡقُواْ فِيهَا سَمِعُواْ لَهَا شَهِيقࣰ ا وَهِيَ تَفُورُ
67:7.en: When they are flung therein they hear its roaring as it boileth up

67:8.ar: تَكَادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَيۡظِۖ كُلَّمَآ أُلۡقِيَ فِيهَا فَوۡجࣱ سَأَلَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ نَذِيرࣱ‏
67:8.en: As it would burst with rage. Whenever a (fresh) host is flung therein the wardens thereof ask them: Came there unto you no warner

67:9.ar: قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ قَدۡ جَآءَنَا نَذِيرࣱ فَكَذَّبۡنَا وَقُلۡنَا مَا نَزَّلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ كَبِيرࣲ‏
67:9.en: They say: Yea, verily, a warner came unto us; but we denied and said: Allah hath naught revealed; ye are in naught but a great error

67:10.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡ كُنَّا نَسۡمَعُ أَوۡ نَعۡقِلُ مَا كُنَّا فِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:10.en: And they say: Had we been wont to listen or have sense, we had not been among the dwellers in the flames

67:11.ar: فَٱعۡتَرَفُواْ بِذَنۢبِهِمۡ فَسُحۡقࣰ ا لِّأَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:11.en: So they acknowledge their sins; but far removed (from mercy) are the dwellers in the flames

67:12.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
67:12.en: Lo! those who fear their Lord in secret, theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward

67:13.ar: وَأَسِرُّواْ قَوۡلَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱجۡهَرُواْ بِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
67:13.en: And keep your opinion secret or proclaim it, lo! He is Knower of all that is in the breasts (of men)

67:14.ar: أَلَا يَعۡلَمُ مَنۡ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
67:14.en: Should He not know what He created? And He is the Subtile, the Aware

67:15.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ ذَلُولࣰ ا فَٱمۡشُواْ فِي مَنَاكِبِهَا وَكُلُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِهِۦۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلنُّشُورُ
67:15.en: He it is Who hath made the earth subservient unto you, so Walk in the paths thereof and eat of His providence. And unto Him will be the resurrection (of the dead)

67:16.ar: ءَأَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يَخۡسِفَ بِكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَمُورُ
67:16.en: Have ye taken security from Him Who is in the heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you when lo! it is convulsed

67:17.ar: أَمۡ أَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حَاصِبࣰ اۖ فَسَتَعۡلَمُونَ كَيۡفَ نَذِيرِ
67:17.en: Or have ye taken security from Him Who is in the heaven that He will not let loose on you a hurricane? But ye shall know the manner of My warning

67:18.ar: وَلَقَدۡ كَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ فَكَيۡفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ
67:18.en: And verily those before them denied, then (see) the manner of My wrath (with them)

67:19.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَى ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَوۡقَهُمۡ صَٰٓفَّٰتࣲ وَيَقۡبِضۡنَۚ مَا يُمۡسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُۚ إِنَّهُۥ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءِۭ بَصِيرٌ
67:19.en: Have they not seen the birds above them spreading out their wings and closing them? Naught upholdeth them save the Beneficent. Lo! He is Seer of all things

67:21.ar: أَمَّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي يَرۡزُقُكُمۡ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَ رِزۡقَهُۥۚ بَل لَّجُّواْ فِي عُتُوࣲّ وَنُفُورٍ
67:21.en: Or who is he that will provide for you if He should withhold His providence? Nay, but they are set in pride and frowardness

67:20.ar: أَمَّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ جُندࣱ لَّكُمۡ يَنصُرُكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِۚ إِنِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ إِلَّا فِي غُرُورٍ
67:20.en: Or who is he that will be an army unto you to help you instead of the Beneficent? The disbelievers are in naught but illusion

17:36.ar: وَلَا تَقۡفُ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۚ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡبَصَرَ وَٱلۡفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنۡهُ مَسۡـُٔولࣰ ا
17:36.en: (O man), follow not that whereof thou hast no knowledge. Lo! the hearing and the sight and the heart - of each of these it will be asked

34:13.ar: يَعۡمَلُونَ لَهُۥ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَٰرِيبَ وَتَمَٰثِيلَ وَجِفَانࣲ كَٱلۡجَوَابِ وَقُدُورࣲ رَّاسِيَٰتٍۚ ٱعۡمَلُوٓاْ ءَالَ دَاوُۥدَ شُكۡرࣰ اۚ وَقَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡ عِبَادِيَ ٱلشَّكُورُ
34:13.en: They made for him what he willed: synagogues and statues, basins like wells and boilers built into the ground. Give thanks, O House of David! Few of My bondmen are thankful

20:124.ar: وَمَنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَن ذِكۡرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ مَعِيشَةࣰ ضَنكࣰ ا وَنَحۡشُرُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ أَعۡمَىٰ
20:124.en: But he who turneth away from remembrance of Me, his will be a narrow life, and I shall bring him blind to the assembly on the Day of Resurrection

20:125.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرۡتَنِيٓ أَعۡمَىٰ وَقَدۡ كُنتُ بَصِيرࣰ ا
20:125.en: He will say: My Lord! Wherefor hast Thou gathered me (hither) blind, when I was wont to see

20:126.ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتۡكَ ءَايَٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَاۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُنسَىٰ
20:126.en: He will say: So (it must be). Our revelations came unto thee but thou didst forget them. In like manner thou art forgotten this Day

18:22.ar: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَٰثَةࣱ رَّابِعُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمۡسَةࣱ سَادِسُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡ رَجۡمَۢا بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۖ وَيَقُولُونَ سَبۡعَةࣱ وَثَامِنُهُمۡ كَلۡبُهُمۡۚ قُل رَّبِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِم مَّا يَعۡلَمُهُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱۗ فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِمۡ إِلَّا مِرَآءࣰ ظَٰهِرࣰ ا وَلَا تَسۡتَفۡتِ فِيهِم مِّنۡهُمۡ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:22.en: (Some) will say: They were three, their dog the fourth, and (some) say: Five, their dog the sixth, guessing at random; and (some) say: Seven, and their dog the eighth. Say (O Muhammad): My Lord is Best Aware of their number. None knoweth them save a few. So contend not concerning them except with an outward contending, and ask not any of them to pronounce concerning them

74:31.ar: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَٰٓئِكَةࣰۖ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا عِدَّتَهُمۡ إِلَّا فِتۡنَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِيَسۡتَيۡقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَيَزۡدَادَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَلَا يَرۡتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَلِيَقُولَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ وَٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلࣰ اۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَمَا هِيَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرَىٰ لِلۡبَشَرِ
74:31.en: We have appointed only angels to be wardens of the Fire, and their number have We made to be a stumbling-block for those who disbelieve; that those to whom the Scripture hath been given may have certainty, and that believers may increase in faith; and that those to whom the Scripture hath been given and believers may not doubt; and that those in whose hearts there is disease, and disbelievers, may say: What meaneth Allah by this similitude? Thus Allah sendeth astray whom He will, and whom He will He guideth. None knoweth the hosts of thy Lord save Him. This is naught else than a Reminder unto mortals

jtJennlrWdE.title: Surat Al-Mulk, Part 6: Verses 22-30
jtJennlrWdE.one_line: Knowledge must lift your head toward guidance: gratitude for hearing, sight and mind, ignoring what does not matter, and applying truth to yourself first.
jtJennlrWdE.summary: Concluding Al-Mulk, he stresses that what unites Muslims is shared theology, and that accepting a truth means accepting what it necessarily implies. Recapping the surah, he explains that its challenges target the very laws of nature: who made provision, gravity and flight work, and who could withhold them. The central verse contrasts one walking face-down with one walking upright on a straight path: knowledge that does not increase guidance was wasted, and obsession with trivia keeps the head down. Knowledge made the companions a civilization where religion and science worked together for a thousand years. The final six commands to the Prophet begin with gratitude for hearing, sight and consciousness, shown by using them well, then the dispersal of humanity in its diversity so we learn from each other. Asked when the Hour comes, the answer is that some knowledge is withheld for our good, like the dog's breed in Al-Kahf or the date of one's death; the Prophet is only a clear warner. Asking what Allah will do with the believers deflects from one's own fate, so he insists religious learning is about yourself, not judging others. The surah ends cyclically: whoever brings back sunken water is the One whose blessings keep coming.

outline.heading: The surah's purpose: required knowledge
outline.gist: The verse reached last week is the surah's centre, showing the purpose of knowledge; the surah deals with theology, not jurisprudence.

outline.heading: Theology unites us; practice may differ
outline.gist: Muslims differ in fiqh and Islam is wide enough for that, but understanding who Allah is unites the ummah.

outline.heading: Truths that carry their conclusions
outline.gist: Accepting that Allah is one necessarily means He has no partner or equal; some statements need further evidence, others do not.

outline.heading: Recap of the first page
outline.gist: Blessing, sovereignty, power, life as opportunity, the flawless heavens, the duality of creation and accountability.

outline.heading: Recap of the second page
outline.gist: He knows His creation; do not feel safe from punishment; walk the earth; who holds the birds aloft but ar-Rahman.

outline.heading: A cluster of names of knowledge
outline.gist: This surah uniquely strings together His names of knowledge so you know you are learning from the source of knowledge.

outline.heading: Who provides if He withholds provision?
outline.gist: The verse is not about where to earn money but about provision itself: if water stopped quenching or seeds stopped growing.

outline.heading: The laws of nature are His
outline.gist: Newton and Einstein described laws they did not make; we know gravity and charge work but not why.

outline.heading: Flight and floating: who put the laws there?
outline.gist: Understanding aerodynamics or buoyancy does not answer who set the laws that we cannot change and cannot survive without.

outline.heading: Face down or walking upright
outline.gist: One walks prone with no view or destination; the other walks upright on a straight path and will arrive.

outline.heading: Knowledge must lead to guidance
outline.gist: If learning does not make the path clearer, it was not helpful; real knowledge lets you rise again however life throws you.

outline.heading: Lift your head from the trivial
outline.gist: Preoccupation with petty details and comfort keeps the head down; see the bigger picture of why you are here.

outline.heading: Knowledge made the companions a civilization
outline.gist: For a thousand years across three continents religion encouraged science, and scholars of religion were scholars of medicine and astronomy.

outline.heading: How Al-Mulk protects in the grave
outline.gist: Living by these facts protects you practically; reading without understanding turns the words into gibberish.

outline.heading: Six commands to say
outline.gist: The surah ends with a cluster of 'say' commands, statements for the Prophet and believers to hold, not only replies to opponents.

outline.heading: Interlude
He raised you gradually and gave you hearing, sight and mind
outline.gist: He brought us up over time and installed hearing, sight and consciousness to process and conclude.

outline.heading: Gratitude means using gifts well
outline.gist: Say alhamdulillah always, but true gratitude for hearing, sight, wealth or health is using them as intended; we will be asked about them.

outline.heading: Umar's prayer to be among the few
outline.gist: Umar asked to be among the few, meaning the few who are grateful; most people feel entitled to what they were given.

outline.heading: Neglected as they neglected
outline.gist: Those who turned from reminders are raised blind; as they ignored the signs, their senses are not restored.

outline.heading: Statements to oneself, not debate lines
outline.gist: Unlike 'say' clusters in debates, these are what the Prophet and believers tell themselves: Allah gave me my faculties and few are grateful.

outline.heading: Dispersed across the earth, gathered back to Him
outline.gist: He scattered humanity like seed, with different races, tongues and traditions, so we learn and grow before returning to Him.

outline.heading: Why only humans need meaning
outline.gist: Apes in the wild are content without purpose; humans have metacognition, and the surge in antidepressants shows existing is not enough.

outline.heading: Diversity is His choice
outline.gist: He chose for us to look and sound different so we learn from each other and value what unites us.

outline.heading: 'When?' is the wrong question
outline.gist: The surah also teaches what we do not need to know; people spend hours arguing about the number of sleepers and their dog's breed.

outline.heading: Nineteen gatekeepers: so what?
outline.gist: Whether the guardians of Hell are nineteen or nineteen thousand changes nothing for you.

outline.heading: Knowledge that is not accessible
outline.gist: Creed texts distinguish knowledge you must learn from knowledge you can never reach, like Allah's essence; pursuing it only confuses.

outline.heading: The one asked knows no more than the asker
outline.gist: The Prophet himself did not know the Hour's timing; knowing one's date of death would only invite procrastination.

outline.heading: Knowledge of it is with Allah; I am only a clear warner
outline.gist: Withheld knowledge is withheld for our good; the double exclusivity signals what matters: we warn, we do not judge or coerce.

outline.heading: Death comes to you; belief demands action
outline.gist: The Quran speaks of death coming to you; accepting that life is an opportunity necessarily means acting on it, or it is hypocrisy.

outline.heading: When they see it drawing near
outline.gist: When the Hour charges toward them, the faces of deniers are distressed and they are told this is what they denied.

outline.heading: The threads come together
outline.gist: This echoes their earlier confession that they had not listened or reasoned: knowledge leads to guidance, its absence to regret.

outline.heading: Interlude
A cyclical surah
outline.gist: The last question is answered by the first verse; he recaps the commands so far.

outline.heading: Whatever happens to us, who will protect you?
outline.gist: The Prophet tells them that whether Allah takes or spares the believers, their concern should be their own punishment.

outline.heading: The three laws of tazkiyah: it's about you
outline.gist: Never hear a lesson and think of someone else; the number one problem with knowledge is preaching without practising.

outline.heading: No time to audit others
outline.gist: Watching for others' mistakes is a disease of the heart; correct people only if they accepted you as a mentor.

outline.heading: He is ar-Rahman: we believe and rely on Him
outline.gist: The fourth mention of ar-Rahman; the conclusion of this knowledge is faith, reliance, and leaving judgment of who is astray to that Day.

outline.heading: If your water sank away, who would bring it?
outline.gist: Another basic law of the earth; the answer is the surah's first word, the One whose unacknowledged blessings keep coming.

outline.heading: Outro

21:47.en: And We set a just balance for the Day of Resurrection so that no soul is wronged in aught. Though it be of the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We bring it. And We suffice for reckoners

Fo8VFsG_UPw.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Hellfire and the Placement of the Scales
Fo8VFsG_UPw.one_line: The last scenes of Jahannam's parade, the first people thrown into it for showing off, and the setting up of the scales of exact justice.
Fo8VFsG_UPw.summary: Continuing the series, he retraces the stages up to the parade of Jahannam and adds the scenes that follow it. Disbelievers are made to admit the Fire is real, people regret the friend who led them away from the Messenger's path, and criminals realise there is no way out. Some are thrown in before any reckoning, and he walks through the narration of the first three: a fighter, a generous man and a Quran carrier who did it all to be called brave, generous and learned. He contrasts them with those kept so far away they never hear it. Then the scales are set up, weighing even what the eye cannot see, and he argues that titles, wealth and status count for nothing there, so it is worth asking why we chase them now. He warns that people can deceive themselves so thoroughly that they walk the wrong way convinced they are doing well. He closes on hope: simple kindness and good character weigh more than anything else, and the narration of the man whose single card of tawhid outweighs ninety-nine scrolls of sins shows that one never knows which good deed will save them.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: from death to the parade of Jahannam
outline.gist: He retraces the stages so far, from the horn and the resurrection through the sun, the shade of the Throne, intercession, the books, the prostration and the display of Jahannam.

outline.heading: Is this not real? The disbelievers before the Fire
outline.gist: Those who denied are shown the Fire and made to admit it is the truth, and are told to taste the punishment.

outline.heading: Regret over the friend who led one astray
outline.gist: People wish they had followed the Messenger's path and had never taken a certain person as a close friend, the one who pulled them away after guidance came; Shaytan always abandons people.

outline.heading: The criminals see the Fire and find no escape
outline.gist: Those who did wrong see Jahannam, know they are about to fall into it and realise it is too late to turn away.

outline.heading: Some thrown in before the reckoning
outline.gist: Even before judgement some are pulled out and cast into the Fire, and a narration names the first people with whom it is kindled.

outline.heading: The fighter who wanted to be called brave
outline.gist: The first is a man who fought and died claiming it was for Allah, and is told he did it to be called courageous, which he already received.

outline.heading: The giver who wanted to be called generous
outline.gist: The second spent his wealth and claims it was for Allah, and is told he did it to be known as generous and got that reputation.

outline.heading: The Quran carrier who wanted a title
outline.gist: The third learned or recited the Quran for the label people would give him. On that day even the prophets can only plead for safety.

outline.heading: Those kept far away from it
outline.gist: The other side of the picture: people who feel no fear or grief because they are so far from Jahannam that they neither see nor hear it.

outline.heading: The scales of exact justice
outline.gist: The scales are set up and even a deed smaller than the eye can see is brought and weighed, with no one wronged. He recalls the narration that no one remembers anyone at certain moments, the first being when the books fly.

outline.heading: Waiting on the scale: heavy wins, light loses
outline.gist: When the scales are set up people hear nothing while they wait to learn whether theirs is heavy or light; heavy means success and light means losing everything.

outline.heading: Titles and status weigh nothing
outline.gist: Professions, wealth, fame and long titles stay behind and each person is called only by name; if none of it counts there, he asks why we fight so hard for it here.

outline.heading: The greatest losers who thought they were doing well
outline.gist: Allah describes those whose efforts were lost while they believed they were doing good; people can walk in the opposite direction convinced it is right.

outline.heading: The masks we lie to ourselves with
outline.gist: We lie to ourselves, believe it and wear mask over mask until we no longer know who we are, and such people are given no weight on that Day.

outline.heading: Good character is the heaviest thing on the scale
outline.gist: Small acts of consideration, like letting a car out or holding a door, make up good character, which is felt more than defined and outweighs everything else on the scale.

outline.heading: The card that outweighed ninety-nine scrolls
outline.gist: The narration of a man with ninety-nine towering scrolls of sins who is saved by a single card of tawhid; you never know which deed will be that card for you.

qJtoSkEU71g.speaker_note: Ramadan Fajr dars series at Muslim Wellness Network; speaks of his own move to London and his medical work
qJtoSkEU71g.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Shade of His Throne (Day 18)
qJtoSkEU71g.one_line: Standing in silence under a near sun, sweating by one's deeds, while seven kinds of people are called into the shade of Allah's Throne.
qJtoSkEU71g.summary: He restates the aim of the series: to make Muslims comfortable with their own mortality, since death should only be a painful transition, yet in his medical work he sees how frightened people are. On the Day of Judgment everyone stands silent, speaking only with permission, because Allah's wrath is at its peak and people had their chance. He argues that our real choice is only about timing: everyone will eventually humble themselves, supplicate and praise Allah, but now it is recorded and rewarded, while then it goes nowhere. The sun is brought close and people sweat according to their deeds, from the ankles to the mouth, while angels call certain people into a shaded area. He walks through the seven whom Allah shades under His Throne: the just leader at any level, from head of state to father, with every betrayal carried as a banner and the failed public leader the worst traitor; the youth raised in worship; the one whose heart is attached to the masjid; two who love each other only for Allah; the one who refuses a powerful, beautiful seducer out of fear of Allah; the one who gives so secretly his left hand does not know; and the one who remembers Allah in spiritual solitude until his eyes fill with tears.

outline.heading: Opening
Why this series: comfort with mortality
outline.gist: Death only ends the chance to do good and repent; for a Muslim doing what he should, it is a painful transition but not something to dread. His work has shown him how far Muslims are from that, so visualizing what is coming should help.

outline.heading: Silence on the plain
outline.gist: After the stages so far, people stand quiet; no one speaks without Allah's permission and only whispers are heard.

outline.heading: Just stand: you had your chance
outline.gist: No objection or opinion is heard that day; Allah's wrath is at its peak and only the oblivious try to speak.

outline.heading: You only choose when
outline.gist: Everyone will praise, prostrate and supplicate; the only choice is whether you do it now, when it is recorded and rewarded, or then, when the dua goes nowhere because the messengers already came.

outline.heading: Labouring when it no longer counts
outline.gist: On that day people are humble, striving and exhausted, as they should have been in this life, but it no longer matters. Make a lot of dua now.

outline.heading: The sun brought near
outline.gist: The sun is brought within a short distance and billions of people from Adam onward sweat according to their deeds, up to the ankles, knees or waist.

outline.heading: Sweat up to the mouth
outline.gist: For some it reaches the chest or mouth so they cannot speak; others whisper dua hoping the Most Merciful accepts it.

outline.heading: A shaded area with special access
outline.gist: Angels call certain people out of the crowd into a shaded area free of sun and sweat, guarded from everyone else. Ask yourself when you would be called.

outline.heading: The just leader
outline.gist: Seven kinds of people are shaded by the Throne, first the just leader: not only a head of state but a father, a principal or a boss, anyone trusted with authority over others.

outline.heading: Every betrayal carried as a banner
outline.gist: Deeds take physical form that day; every betrayer carries a banner naming his betrayal that follows him wherever he goes, and the same holds for every sin and every good deed.

outline.heading: The worst traitor
outline.gist: No betrayal is worse than that of a public leader who did not exhaust every resource to serve his people. Were you just with whatever authority Allah gave you?

outline.heading: Longing for the shade
outline.gist: If Ramadan hunger is hard, imagine the blazing sun with nothing to drink, wishing one of these categories applied to you.

outline.heading: The youth raised in worship
outline.gist: Someone who spent the energetic, capable years of youth learning the Quran and drawing near to Allah, not only coming back when old and tired.

outline.heading: The heart attached to the masjid
outline.gist: Like a fish that must return to water, they keep coming back; the masjid is the hub where Muslims are served, and being connected to it gives you a compass in life.

outline.heading: Two who love each other for Allah
outline.gist: They meet and part for Allah alone, with no business, wealth or kinship tying them, and walk to the shade in pairs.

outline.heading: Refusing the powerful and beautiful
outline.gist: The seducer is described as powerful and beautiful so that the only reason left to refuse is reverence for Allah, not fear of scandal; few besides Yusuf will manage this.

outline.heading: Charity so secret the left hand does not know
outline.gist: He went out of his way to hide his giving from everyone, even parts of himself, as carefully as others hide their sins.

outline.heading: Remembering Allah alone until tears flow
outline.gist: Solitude is spiritual, not physical: you can be alone with Allah among millions at Hajj, or in your room hoping someone sees you. When the heart holds only Allah and the eyes fill with tears, you are among the seven.

outline.heading: Those left standing
outline.gist: Once the seven groups have gone, everyone else stays in the sun for a long time; those who reach the shade find everything after it easier.

14:21.en: They all come forth unto their Lord. Then those who were despised say unto those who were scornful: We were unto you a following, can ye then avert from us aught of Allah's doom? They say: Had Allah guided us, we should have guided you. Whether we rage or patiently endure is (now) all one for us; we have no place of refuge

34:31.en: And those who disbelieve say: We believe not in this Qur'an nor in that which was before it; but oh, if thou couldst see, when the wrong-doers are brought up before their Lord, how they cast the blame one to another; how those who were despised (in the earth) say unto those who were proud: But for you, we should have been believers

34:32.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُوٓاْ أَنَحۡنُ صَدَدۡنَٰكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَكُمۖ بَلۡ كُنتُم مُّجۡرِمِينَ
34:32.en: Those who were proud say unto those who were despised: Did we drive you away from the guidance after it had come unto you? Nay, but ye were guilty

34:33.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ بَلۡ مَكۡرُ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذۡ تَأۡمُرُونَنَآ أَن نَّكۡفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَنَجۡعَلَ لَهُۥٓ أَندَادࣰ اۚ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ فِيٓ أَعۡنَاقِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۖ هَلۡ يُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
34:33.en: Those who were despised say unto those who were proud: Nay but (it was your) scheming night and day, when ye commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals unto Him. And they are filled with remorse when they behold the doom; and We place carcans on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they requited aught save what they used to do

b648oDp89dE.speaker: adnan
b648oDp89dE.speaker_note: episode of his own Ramadan post-Fajr series on the stages of the Hereafter; single voice in his usual style
b648oDp89dE.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Viewing of the Hellfire
b648oDp89dE.one_line: After the books are handed out, leaders and followers turn on each other, then Jahannam is paraded before humanity: where will you be?
b648oDp89dE.summary: This dars picks up the journey through the Day of Judgement. He first retraces the stages covered so far, from the grave and the two blasts of the horn to the scorching sun, the shade of the Throne, the search for an intercessor and the start of judgement, then the call to prostrate and the books flying into people's hands. He pauses on narrations naming people Allah will not look at, stressing that the worst sins are those committed with no pressure at all: a king who lies, an old man who commits zina, a poor man who is arrogant. He then reads the Quranic scenes in which followers and their leaders argue, disown each other and wish for a second chance, insisting that "I was only following orders" will not work, and that shirk is far subtler than bowing to a stone. The tone then shifts to the moment Jahannam is brought out: nations fall to their knees, it nearly bursts with rage at arrogant humans, and people can only glance at it from the corner of the eye. He asks the audience to spend Ramadan asking where they will be standing at that moment, among the terrified or among those far away who never hear a sound of it.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: from the grave to the start of judgement
outline.gist: He retraces the earlier stages: the grave, the two blasts of the horn, the collapse of the universe, the sun drawing near, the shade of the Throne and the Prophet's intercession that starts the reckoning.

outline.heading: Allah's coming, the call to prostrate and the flying books
outline.gist: Allah and the angels come, people are called to prostrate and only some can, and then the records fly into people's hands.

outline.heading: Those Allah will not look at: sin with no pressure behind it
outline.gist: Narrations about people Allah will not look at, including the lying king, the elderly fornicator and the arrogant poor man; their sins have no motive or excuse, which is what makes them so ugly. He adds that those who had much in this world will have least, except those who gave it away.

outline.heading: No excuse of following orders: leaders and followers argue
outline.gist: The weak ask those they followed to carry part of the punishment; the arrogant reply that they are all in it together and that there is no escape whether they panic or endure.

outline.heading: Disowning each other and wishing to go back
outline.gist: Leaders deny any link to their followers once they see the punishment, every tie is cut, and the followers wish for a return to the world to disown them in turn.

outline.heading: The weak blame the strong for their disbelief
outline.gist: The followers say they would have believed but for their leaders, who answer that they never blocked guidance, while the followers point to the constant scheming that pushed them to set up rivals to Allah.

outline.heading: Shirk runs deeper than idols
outline.gist: Associating partners with Allah happens on subtle spiritual and intellectual levels, not only by bowing to stone; many do it without knowing. Both sides hide their regret when they see the punishment.

outline.heading: Jahannam brought out: where will you be?
outline.gist: The tone shifts as Jahannam is brought into view and people suddenly remember all their choices when remembering is no longer of use; he asks whether you will be among the onlookers or safe in the shade of the Throne.

outline.heading: Paraded before them: every nation on its knees
outline.gist: Jahannam is displayed before the disbelievers and every nation falls to its knees, not by command but because fear buckles their legs.

outline.heading: Jahannam's rage at the arrogant creature
outline.gist: Jahannam almost tears itself apart in fury at small, weak humans who dared to disobey Allah when it would never dare to.

outline.heading: Its roar from afar and the glance from the corner of the eye
outline.gist: People hear its raging and exhaling from a distance, and those on their knees only dare look at it sideways, in complete humiliation.

outline.heading: The seventy thousand reins
outline.gist: He returns to the question of where we will be, and describes the narration of Jahannam dragged by seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels, throwing sparks as large as castles.

outline.heading: Those who never hear it
outline.gist: The people promised the best are kept far away, unaware of the horror, enjoying the shade and each other's company while others watch.

69:25.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
69:25.en: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: Oh, would that I had not been given my book

69:26.en: And knew not what my reckoning

69:27.en: Oh, would that it had been death

69:28.en: My wealth hath not availed me

69:29.en: My power hath gone from me

84:10.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهۡرِهِۦ
84:10.en: But whoso is given his account behind his back

84:12.en: And be thrown to scorching fire

17:13.ar: وَكُلَّ إِنسَٰنٍ أَلۡزَمۡنَٰهُ طَٰٓئِرَهُۥ فِي عُنُقِهِۦۖ وَنُخۡرِجُ لَهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا يَلۡقَىٰهُ مَنشُورًا
17:13.en: And every man's augury have We fastened to his own neck, and We shall bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find wide open

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا
17:14.en: (And it will be said unto him): Read thy Book. Thy soul sufficeth as reckoner against thee this day

18:49.ar: وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ فَتَرَى ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَٰوَيۡلَتَنَا مَالِ هَٰذَا ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةࣰ وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّآ أَحۡصَىٰهَاۚ وَوَجَدُواْ مَا عَمِلُواْ حَاضِرࣰ اۗ وَلَا يَظۡلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدࣰ ا
18:49.en: And the Book is placed, and thou seest the guilty fearful of that which is therein, and they say: What kind of a Book is this that leaveth not a small thing nor a great thing but hath counted it! And they find all that they did confronting them, and thy Lord wrongeth no-one

3:30.ar: يَوۡمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ مَّا عَمِلَتۡ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ مُّحۡضَرࣰ ا وَمَا عَمِلَتۡ مِن سُوٓءࣲ تَوَدُّ لَوۡ أَنَّ بَيۡنَهَا وَبَيۡنَهُۥٓ أَمَدَۢا بَعِيدࣰ اۗ وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسَهُۥۗ وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
3:30.en: On the Day when every soul will find itself confronted with all that it hath done of good and all that it hath done of evil (every soul) will long that there might be a mighty space of distance between it and that (evil). Allah biddeth you beware of Him. And Allah is Full of Pity for (His) bondmen

45:29.ar: هَٰذَا كِتَٰبُنَا يَنطِقُ عَلَيۡكُم بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسۡتَنسِخُ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
45:29.en: This Our Book pronounceth against you with truth. Lo! We have caused (all) that ye did to be recorded

0X-spVJCoBQ.title: Stages of the Hereafter: Receiving the Records (Day 20)
0X-spVJCoBQ.one_line: Allah's coming with the angels, the call to prostrate that some cannot answer, and the books of deeds flying into right hands, left hands and behind backs.
0X-spVJCoBQ.summary: He asks whether we truly qualify as the Prophet's ummah, since his intercession helps only those who are really his. Then comes the most magnificent event: angels arrive rank upon rank filling the horizon, the Throne carried by eight, and Allah comes in a way no one can describe. He explains the two readings of the shin being uncovered, either a revelation of Allah's glory or things turning suddenly grave, and then everyone is called to prostrate. Those who refused when they were healthy find their backs fused and cannot bend; the worldly law is reversed, so the raised head is the humiliated one and the head on the ground the honoured one. The books then fly from under the Throne, and in that moment no one recognises anyone. The one given his book in the right hand returns joyfully to his family, while the one given it in the left wishes death had been the end and finds his wealth and status gone. He stresses that only you and Allah truly care about you, and that your book is still being edited through every hardship until it lands in your hand. Some receive it behind their backs, having known all this and ignored it. Every thought and joke is recorded, and you are asked to judge yourself.

outline.heading: Opening
The journey so far
outline.gist: Death, the barzakh, the second blow, the chaos, the collapse of the universe, the near sun and the shade of the Throne.

outline.heading: Everything waits for the Prophet
outline.gist: In the weight of the moment no one even remembers to go to him first; when they do, he prostrates under the Throne and his intercession is accepted.

outline.heading: Are you truly of his ummah?
outline.gist: His call benefits those who are truly his; whether our lives meet that criterion needs focus and honest revision.

outline.heading: Angels rank upon rank
outline.gist: The most magnificent event: lines of angels advance like an army until they fill every horizon.

outline.heading: Allah comes, and the Throne is carried by eight
outline.gist: What Allah's coming means, no one knows or should speculate about, since He is not bound by time or space; we will only know at that moment.

outline.heading: The shin uncovered: two readings
outline.gist: It may refer to something specific to Allah's glory, or to an Arabic idiom for a matter baring its fangs and becoming deadly serious.

outline.heading: The call to prostrate
outline.gist: The long wait suddenly turns intense; seeing Allah's glory with their own senses, everyone wants to prostrate and all are called to do so.

outline.heading: Those who cannot bend
outline.gist: Those who were called to prostrate in life while healthy and refused find their backs turned into a single rigid piece, eyes humbled.

outline.heading: The raised head becomes the humiliated one
outline.gist: In this world the head held high signals honour; that day the law flips, and those able to put their heads on the ground are the honoured ones.

outline.heading: Prostrate now, in this world
outline.gist: They long to show where their loyalty lies but are stuck with their backs up, the only heads raised; the time to do it is in this life.

outline.heading: The books fly
outline.gist: After witnessing Allah, His Throne and angels, the records are spread and the sky turns dark with books. Aisha was told of three moments when no one remembers anyone.

outline.heading: Right hand or left?
outline.gist: No empathy or interest in others is left; everyone is fully absorbed in where their book will land.

outline.heading: The book in the right hand
outline.gist: His reckoning is easy and, after zoning everyone out, he turns back to his family satisfied and happy.

outline.heading: Here, read my book!
outline.gist: He calls on others to look: Allah forgave what he feared, and this day is what his life was aimed at. He lives a pleasing life in a high garden, told to eat and drink for what he sent ahead.

outline.heading: The book in the left hand
outline.gist: Those who lived with blind hearts are forgotten as they forgot. He never thought of being accountable, wishes death had been the end, and finds his wealth, fame and followers useless.

outline.heading: Only you and Allah truly care
outline.gist: We are insignificant to everyone but ourselves and Allah; others care only for a limited time, and a moment is coming when no one cares at all.

outline.heading: Your book is edited until it reaches your hand
outline.gist: Until the book lands, every hardship, pain and long wait removes sins, which is why some who had a terrible path end well. Once it is in your hand, it is fixed.

outline.heading: The book behind the back
outline.gist: Those who knew in this life how the books are given but ignored it panic and hide the left hand behind their back, like a child dodging the teacher's ruler.

outline.heading: Judge yourself
outline.gist: They wish for destruction, having once been happy among family. You will read your own book and tell Allah with a clear conscience whether you deserve what comes next.

outline.heading: Even the joke is written
outline.gist: Every thought and every throwaway joke, even one the other person never heard, is in the book.

outline.heading: A warning out of mercy
outline.gist: No one is wronged; good deeds are there and bad ones you wish were far away. Allah warns us of Himself out of love, and His record speaks the truth.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Those who refused to prostrate in life cannot prostrate then; do it now.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Receiving the records, reading and judging oneself, with every thought and joke recorded.

quran.point: Your Lord comes with the angels rank upon rank.
Eight carry the Throne of your Lord that day.
The day the shin is uncovered and they are called to prostrate but cannot, having refused when they were sound.
When the records are spread open.
Given the book in the right hand, he has an easy reckoning and returns to his family joyful.
Here, read my book! I knew I would meet my account; a pleasing life in a high garden; eat and drink for what you sent ahead.
You forgot Our signs, so today you are forgotten.
Given his book in the left hand, he wishes death had been the end; his wealth did not help and his authority is gone.
Given the book behind his back, he calls for destruction, having been happy among his people.
Read your book; you are enough as a reckoner against yourself today.
The book leaves nothing small or great unrecorded, and no one is wronged.
Each soul finds its good present and wishes its evil were far away; Allah warns you of Himself and is kind to His servants.
This record of Ours speaks the truth; We were recording all that you did.

hadith.gist: Aisha asked whether people will remember their loved ones on the Day of Judgment; the Prophet said in three places no one remembers anyone, among them when the books fly, until one knows whether his falls in his right or left hand.
Hardship and pain that befall a believer remove his sins.

maxims: The only two who truly care about you: you and Allah.
Your book is edited until it lands in your hand.
Prostrate now, or be the only head raised.

stories.who: A child hiding his hand from the teacher's ruler
stories.point: Those who knew the rules but ignored them hide their left hand behind their back, hoping to dodge the book.

takeaways: Review your life honestly to be sure you truly belong to the Prophet's ummah.
Prostrate to Allah now, while you are healthy and able.
Prepare your book so you can hand it around with joy, and remember it is still being edited until then.
Watch even your thoughts and jokes, since everything is recorded.
Bear hardships knowing they remove sins before the records are handed out.

78:18.ar: يَوۡمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَتَأۡتُونَ أَفۡوَاجࣰ ا
78:18.en: A day when the trumpet is blown and ye come in multitudes

20:108.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِيَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُۥۖ وَخَشَعَتِ ٱلۡأَصۡوَاتُ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ فَلَا تَسۡمَعُ إِلَّا هَمۡسࣰ ا
20:108.en: On that day they follow the summoner who deceiveth not, and voices are hushed for the Beneficent, and thou hearest but a faint murmur

19:85.ar: يَوۡمَ نَحۡشُرُ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَفۡدࣰ ا
19:85.en: On the day when We shall gather the righteous unto the Beneficent, a goodly company

19:86.ar: وَنَسُوقُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وِرۡدࣰ ا
19:86.en: And drive the guilty unto hell, a weary herd

6:23.ar: ثُمَّ لَمۡ تَكُن فِتۡنَتُهُمۡ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُواْ وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشۡرِكِينَ
6:23.en: Then will they have no contention save that they will say: By Allah, our Lord, we never were idolaters

6:24.ar: ٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ كَذَبُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡۚ وَضَلَّ عَنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ
6:24.en: See how they lie against themselves, and (how) the thing which they devised hath failed them

17:97.ar: وَمَن يَهۡدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدِۖ وَمَن يُضۡلِلۡ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِهِۦۖ وَنَحۡشُرُهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمۡ عُمۡيࣰ ا وَبُكۡمࣰ ا وَصُمࣰّ اۖ مَّأۡوَىٰهُمۡ جَهَنَّمُۖ كُلَّمَا خَبَتۡ زِدۡنَٰهُمۡ سَعِيرࣰ ا
17:97.en: And he whom Allah guideth, he is led aright; while, as for him whom He sendeth astray, for them thou wilt find no protecting friends beside Him, and We shall assemble them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf; their habitation will be hell; whenever it abateth, We increase the flame for them

20:124.ar: وَمَنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَن ذِكۡرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ مَعِيشَةࣰ ضَنكࣰ ا وَنَحۡشُرُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ أَعۡمَىٰ
20:124.en: But he who turneth away from remembrance of Me, his will be a narrow life, and I shall bring him blind to the assembly on the Day of Resurrection

20:125.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرۡتَنِيٓ أَعۡمَىٰ وَقَدۡ كُنتُ بَصِيرࣰ ا
20:125.en: He will say: My Lord! Wherefor hast Thou gathered me (hither) blind, when I was wont to see

20:126.ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتۡكَ ءَايَٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَاۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُنسَىٰ
20:126.en: He will say: So (it must be). Our revelations came unto thee but thou didst forget them. In like manner thou art forgotten this Day

70:4.ar: تَعۡرُجُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيۡهِ فِي يَوۡمࣲ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُۥ خَمۡسِينَ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ‏
70:4.en: (Whereby) the angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him in a Day whereof the span is fifty thousand years

20:102.ar: يَوۡمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِۚ وَنَحۡشُرُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ زُرۡقࣰ ا
20:102.en: The day when the Trumpet is blown. On that day we assemble the guilty white-eyed (with terror)

20:103.ar: يَتَخَٰفَتُونَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا عَشۡرࣰ ا
20:103.en: Murmuring among themselves: Ye have tarried but ten (days)

20:104.ar: نَّحۡنُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذۡ يَقُولُ أَمۡثَلُهُمۡ طَرِيقَةً إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا يَوۡمࣰ ا
20:104.en: We are Best Aware of what they utter when their best in conduct say: Ye have tarried but a day

23:112.ar: قَٰلَ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ عَدَدَ سِنِينَ
23:112.en: He will say: How long tarried ye in the earth, counting by years

23:113.ar: قَالُواْ لَبِثۡنَا يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمࣲ فَسۡـَٔلِ ٱلۡعَآدِّينَ
23:113.en: They will say: We tarried by a day or part of a day. Ask of those who keep count

23:114.ar: قَٰلَ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ اۖ لَّوۡ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
23:114.en: He will say: Ye tarried but a little if ye only knew

79:46.ar: كَأَنَّهُمۡ يَوۡمَ يَرَوۡنَهَا لَمۡ يَلۡبَثُوٓاْ إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوۡ ضُحَىٰهَا
79:46.en: On the day when they behold it, it will be as if they had but tarried for an evening or the morn thereof

10:45.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يَحۡشُرُهُمۡ كَأَن لَّمۡ يَلۡبَثُوٓاْ إِلَّا سَاعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّهَارِ يَتَعَارَفُونَ بَيۡنَهُمۡۚ قَدۡ خَسِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِلِقَآءِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُهۡتَدِينَ
10:45.en: And on the day when He shall gather them together, (when it will seem) as though they had tarried but an hour of the day, recognising one another, those will verily have perished who denied the meeting with Allah and were not guided

unV0eY0T50o.speaker_note: Ramadan Fajr dars series at Muslim Wellness Network; recaps his own previous lessons on the two blows
unV0eY0T50o.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Gathering on the Day of Judgment (Day 17)
unV0eY0T50o.one_line: How people are gathered on the Day of Judgment, in what forms, for how long, and why life will feel like a single hour.
unV0eY0T50o.summary: He describes the gathering: everyone arrives barefoot and unclothed, yet the terror is so great that no one even notices, as the Prophet told Aisha. People follow the caller in silence; the righteous arrive as an honoured delegation while criminals are driven like convicts and try to lie their way out. Ibrahim is the first to be clothed, and the Prophet's vision of garments of different lengths shows that what covers us that day is our faith and deeds. The arrogant are gathered the size of ants and trampled, some walk, some ride, some are dragged on their faces, the one who ignored Allah's signs is raised blind and forgotten, and those who loved one another for Allah stand on raised places the prophets admire. With no word of what comes next, the standing can last fifty thousand years, though for a believer it passes like a short prayer. He asks listeners to imagine standing as long as they lived just to regret how they spent it. The Quran repeatedly shows people insisting they lived only ten days, a day or an hour, and he argues they are sincere: life already shrinks to a few snapshots in memory, so it should not be wasted.

outline.heading: Opening
Gathered barefoot and unclothed
outline.gist: People are gathered in the natural state Allah created them in, bringing nothing from their previous life.

outline.heading: Too terrified to notice
outline.gist: Aisha asked whether men and women would look at each other; the Prophet said the matter is far too severe. Instincts that would normally dominate do not even register, which shows the magnitude of that day.

outline.heading: Following the caller in silence
outline.gist: People come in crowds following the voice that calls them, with only whispers heard; the righteous arrive as an honoured delegation, like a state visit.

outline.heading: Criminals driven like convicts, and their lie
outline.gist: Wrongdoers are herded like prisoners and, faced with how wrong they were, can only deny what they did. Ibrahim is the first to be given a garment to cover himself.

outline.heading: Garments of different lengths
outline.gist: In a vision the Prophet saw people in shirts reaching only the neck, the chest, the stomach or the knees, while one dragged his on the ground.

outline.heading: The arrogant gathered as ants
outline.gist: The garments stand for the faith and deeds one brings. Those who thought themselves better than others are gathered the size of ants and trampled unnoticed.

outline.heading: Walking, riding or dragged on their faces
outline.gist: Some are gathered walking, some riding because of their raised status, and some moving face-down toward the ground.

outline.heading: Raised blind and forgotten
outline.gist: The one who turned from Allah's signs asks why he was raised blind; just as he forgot them, he is overlooked that day.

outline.heading: Those who loved for Allah's sake
outline.gist: Some stand on raised places visible to all, often in twos and threes: people who loved each other for Allah, whose position even prophets admire.

outline.heading: Picture your own state
outline.gist: Imagine leaving the grave, finding your family, staying calm as the universe falls apart, covered rather than exposed, not shrunk by arrogance or walking face-down.

outline.heading: Fifty thousand years of waiting
outline.gist: No one tells you what comes next and nothing is official; the standing lasts fifty thousand years, yet for the believer it feels like a quick prayer.

outline.heading: Time is relative: the Day of Standing
outline.gist: The experience ranges from the length of two short rakaat to fifty thousand years, which is why the Day is named after the standing.

outline.heading: Standing as long as you lived
outline.gist: Even eighty years sits near the short end of that range, yet imagine standing your whole lifespan just to regret how you used the time you had.

outline.heading: We stayed only ten days
outline.gist: A major theme of the Day is that people cannot tell how long they lived; the criminals, blue with dread, whisper that it was only ten.

outline.heading: A day or part of a day
outline.gist: The most accurate of them says a single day, and asked how many years they lived, they say a day or less and tell Allah to ask those who kept count. The reply: you stayed only a little, if only you had known then.

outline.heading: Life as a few snapshots
outline.gist: It will seem like an evening or a morning. Already now you can summarise your life in a minute or two, so their sense of a short life is sincere, not a lie.

outline.heading: An hour to get acquainted
outline.gist: Life will feel like an hour spent getting to know each other. Time is fragile, and fifty thousand years is longer than all of meaningful human history.

AA7dRXGkqF0.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Second Blow of the Horn (Day 13)
AA7dRXGkqF0.one_line: The second blow raises everyone from their graves in panic; he asks listeners to visualize it and to build families that stand together on that day.
AA7dRXGkqF0.summary: After the long silence, Allah revives the angel of the horn and the second blow brings every creature out of the grave in panic, as Ya-Sin, Al-Hajj, An-Najm, Qaf and An-Nazi'at describe. He defines the Day of Judgment as the moment Allah's displeasure with His creation peaks: He keeps granting time for repentance as long as a few people still call others back to Him, which is why the end is still far. Citing an early scholar who softened hardened hearts by having people imagine these scenes, he asks the audience to visualize waking after perhaps millions of years, watching the soil rush back into veins, bones and even fingerprints, instantly rather than gradually. You might expect to embrace the family buried around you, but most will flee from parents, spouses and children, while those who worshipped together hold on to each other and the one who strayed runs alone. He urges parents to prepare their families for that day above all else, since past choices become reality the moment we leave the grave. He ends as the laws of the universe begin to break: the sun wrapped up, stars falling, mountains like carded wool.

outline.heading: Opening
The angel of the horn revived
outline.gist: After the silence lasts as long as Allah wills, He gives life to the angel of the horn, the only living thing, and commands him to blow.

outline.heading: Who raised us from our sleep?
outline.gist: Those who denied this moment realise they were unprepared; every prophet and every faith spoke of a day of resurrection, and one call gathers everyone.

outline.heading: Rising in panic
outline.gist: Every creature emerges terrified except whom Allah spares, coming because they are commanded, not by choice. Nursing mothers abandon their infants and people look drunk though they are not.

outline.heading: Do you laugh instead of weeping?
outline.gist: The approaching Day is rushing near and only Allah can avert it, yet people treat it with amusement and indifference.

outline.heading: The Day when creation's time runs out
outline.gist: The Day of Judgment is when Allah's displeasure with His creation peaks. He keeps granting time for repentance as long as a few people still call others back to Him; only when no one is left does the Hour come, which is why it is still far.

outline.heading: The call from a near place
outline.gist: All creation hears the blast in truth, the earth splits open and they rush out; gathering them is easy for Allah.

outline.heading: The quake and the one that follows
outline.gist: The first quake put everyone to sleep and the second wakes them, with hearts trembling and eyes cast down; deniers call it a losing return.

outline.heading: An early scholar who taught people to visualize
outline.gist: One shout brings everyone onto a sleepless plain. An early scholar who found people's hearts hardened would gather them at night to imagine these scenes, and was invited to teach the method in other lands.

outline.heading: Imagine waking from the grave
outline.gist: We are visual creatures who need to picture what we hear. Imagine waking after hundreds, thousands or millions of years in the barzakh.

outline.heading: Your body rebuilt from the soil
outline.gist: You watch the soil rush back into veins, muscles and bones. The first creation was gradual, like a plant growing, but the second is instantaneous, and Allah can restore even the fingertips.

outline.heading: Rising among family, then fleeing them
outline.gist: You emerge covered in earth among relatives buried beside you and expect to embrace them after the lost years, but instead people run from their siblings, parents, spouses and children.

outline.heading: The rush toward the caller
outline.gist: Amid complete chaos the disbelievers race toward the caller saying this is a hard day, yet some people are holding on to one another.

outline.heading: Those who worshipped together stand together
outline.gist: Friends become enemies except the God-conscious. Families who worshipped Allah together hold hands and steady one another, while the one who strayed runs alone.

outline.heading: Prepare your family for that day
outline.gist: Your family will be what you and your spouse made it. Prepare your children for the day you most need your unit, because the hardships have not even begun.

outline.heading: We are the stars of this film
outline.gist: This is not a blockbuster to watch with popcorn; it will happen to us. The moment we leave the grave our past choices become reality and there is no renegotiating them.

outline.heading: The laws of the universe break
outline.gist: The sun is wrapped up, the stars fall and burn out, and mountains drift like carded wool. Matter and its laws change, and we are frightened by a world that no longer behaves as we know it.

9:53.ar: قُلۡ أَنفِقُواْ طَوۡعًا أَوۡ كَرۡهࣰ ا لَّن يُتَقَبَّلَ مِنكُمۡ إِنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
9:53.en: Say: Pay (your contribution), willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you. Lo! ye were ever froward folk

9:54.ar: وَمَا مَنَعَهُمۡ أَن تُقۡبَلَ مِنۡهُمۡ نَفَقَٰتُهُمۡ إِلَّآ أَنَّهُمۡ كَفَرُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَبِرَسُولِهِۦ وَلَا يَأۡتُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ إِلَّا وَهُمۡ كُسَالَىٰ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَ إِلَّا وَهُمۡ كَٰرِهُونَ
9:54.en: And naught preventeth that their contributions should be accepted from them save that they have disbelieved in Allah and in His messenger, and they come not to worship save as idlers, and pay not (their contribution) save reluctantly

d1XUgAyE0ho.speaker: adnan
d1XUgAyE0ho.speaker_note: Continues the series on the pledge from last week and says he has served at this masjid for ten years.
d1XUgAyE0ho.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Second Article, Committing Wealth (Part 2)
d1XUgAyE0ho.one_line: Committing wealth starts with zakat paid properly, locally and centrally; then sadaqah for community needs, without Western-style gala fundraising.
d1XUgAyE0ho.summary: His second khutbah on the pledge's second article, committing wealth. He frames the series with last October's events, a wake-up call that has pushed Muslims in the West to re-examine how and why they live. The Prophet asked for the pledge not for himself, since he kept Madinah simple rather than build an imperial capital, but for the benefit of those who gave it, and it is a pledge already proven to work. Committing wealth starts with zakat, second only to salah: Abu Bakr fought those who would no longer pay it centrally, and without centralized wealth no ummah can function. Zakat is owed first to the needy where you live, and he admits he once doubted that his city has widows, single mothers and refugees who cannot make ends meet. Giving is only half the work; the rest of life is spent hoping deeds are accepted, and the hypocrites' unwilling giving was refused. Sadaqah then fills the community's gaps, as at Tabuk. In the second khutbah he rejects gala fundraising as foreign to Islam because it shuts out the man with a handful of dates, tells of the companion who gave his honour as charity, and asks the community to make its masjid self-sustaining.

outline.heading: Opening
October as a wake-up call
outline.gist: He finishes the second article because last October, though it started nothing that had not been happening for 75 years, shook Muslims in the West more than a Middle East desensitized by years of turmoil, and is pushing them to re-evaluate how and why they live.

outline.heading: Asking for a pledge, seeking nothing for himself
outline.gist: See the moment from the side of the one who asked: it takes a lot to ask people for a pledge, and the Prophet was not after power, wealth or status, even when it was offered to him on a golden platter.

outline.heading: Madinah never became an imperial capital
outline.gist: He could have rebuilt Madinah or Makkah like Damascus or Constantinople, the capitals of the empires of the day, but kept it simple and invested in people, principles and values. Madinah never took on the castles and luxury of a medieval capital; only when the empire lost his teachings did it fall into those mistakes and decline.

outline.heading: A pledge for your benefit, not His
outline.gist: Asking for a pledge to benefit yourself is one thing; asking for one that benefits only the giver is grace and generosity. Allah's decree happens whether we stand by it or not, and He needs nothing from us.

outline.heading: A pledge already proven to work
outline.gist: These pledges save us individually and collectively, and unlike most pledges this one was tried and succeeded. The first article was to listen, adhere and follow to the best of your ability, not to treat Islam as a part-time gym membership or a consultant.

outline.heading: The essence of committing wealth is zakat
outline.gist: When the Prophet spoke of committing wealth, zakat came first. His private view: a functioning masjid should never need to ask so generous a community to pay its bills, so if it has to ask, it must be failing.

outline.heading: The Prophet asked only to level up
outline.gist: The Prophet asked for money only to move his society forward: buying wells so the community was self-sufficient in water, equipping an army to defend Madinah. Running costs were covered automatically because everyone paid zakat and gave on an ongoing basis.

outline.heading: The Muhajirun had already given everything
outline.gist: The people of Makkah did not need this pledge: for a full decade they had followed him to the letter and given all their wealth, some even their homes. The pledge was for those newly accepting Islam.

outline.heading: Core or newcomer: there is no third option
outline.gist: Are you core or new? The core are ten steps ahead, already giving beyond their capacity and teaching others; newcomers must pledge. There is no third option in the deen.

outline.heading: The hypocrites' giving was refused
outline.gist: The only third option is the hypocrites of At-Tawbah 9:53-54, told that their spending, willing or unwilling, would not be accepted, because they never truly committed, prayed lazily and gave only when pushed. Giving is only half; it has to be accepted.

outline.heading: Spend your life on acceptance
outline.gist: You have no proof that anything you have done was accepted. Doing the articles is the step taken right at the start; offer them quickly, then spend the rest of your life trying to make sure Allah accepts deeds that lack sincerity and impact.

outline.heading: Second only to salah: Abu Bakr and the refusers
outline.gist: Zakat must be properly calculated and is second only to salah. After the Prophet's death Abu Bakr sent armies against those who would no longer pay it centrally; most had not left Islam, they simply refused to hand it over.

outline.heading: Without centralized wealth there is no ummah
outline.gist: You do not get to decide how to practise Islam. Without zakat there is no nation or state, and masajid must fundraise petty sums every year because our communities have no financial centralization, so zakat must be gathered centrally.

outline.heading: Zakat goes first to your own city
outline.gist: All four schools agree zakat may go elsewhere only if the needy where you live do not need it. Individuals cannot find every needy person, so the community is collectively liable; he admits that before 2018-19 he did not believe such need existed here.

outline.heading: Widows, single mothers and refugees here
outline.gist: He saw with his own eyes widows, single mothers and refugees in the city who cannot make ends meet and do not ask, far more than he thought, especially since Covid. There is no barakah in a community that does not care for its weak, so learn to calculate your zakat.

outline.heading: After zakat: fill the community's gaps
outline.gist: Pay zakat on time, with a specialist if you have investments; then see what the community lacks and give collectively. Before Tabuk the companions were so poor that they brought handfuls of dates, half the food in their homes.

outline.heading: Tabuk: the companion nothing could harm
outline.gist: A thousand kilometres north against the Romans needed a proper army, and one companion gave so much that the Prophet said nothing he did afterwards could harm him. Expertise, energy, youth and volunteers do not go far without wealth.

outline.heading: Interlude
Each person owes their own zakat
outline.gist: Zakat has to be prioritized, and each person is obligated to work out their own whether or not anyone runs a session for them. Second, the community's institutions should not have to keep asking for money; the way things run now is not healthy.

outline.heading: The tuxedo-club fundraiser
outline.gist: Committing wealth should happen automatically. Western galas, where you pay $500 to dress up, eat and be flattered for being wealthy, belong to a different culture and mentality of wealth.

outline.heading: The minbar way: state the need and account for it
outline.gist: On the minbar you state what is needed, people give and you move on, with accountability and transparency so the wealth visibly serves Muslims. He has disliked fundraising dinners throughout his ten years here: the method itself is wrong.

outline.heading: The man with a handful of dates
outline.gist: The dinners lack the feel of community because the man with a handful of dates cannot attend. The Prophet praised whoever brought even one date.

outline.heading: The companion who gave his honour as charity
outline.gist: A poor companion with nothing to give prayed at night that he gave as charity his forgiveness of every wrong any Muslim had done him. The next morning the Prophet asked for the one who gave last night and swore Allah had accepted it; everyone puts in what they have, and that is how nations are built.

outline.heading: The community owes its spaces
outline.gist: A place of worship must sustain itself before the community can plan schools, gyms, academies and social spaces. It belongs to the community, not to him, and has to be run as a team.

outline.heading: Outro
