14:22.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لَمَّا قُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمۡ وَعۡدَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَوَعَدتُّكُمۡ فَأَخۡلَفۡتُكُمۡۖ وَمَا كَانَ لِيَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّن سُلۡطَٰنٍ إِلَّآ أَن دَعَوۡتُكُمۡ فَٱسۡتَجَبۡتُمۡ لِيۖ فَلَا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۖ مَّآ أَنَا۠ بِمُصۡرِخِكُمۡ وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُصۡرِخِيَّ إِنِّي كَفَرۡتُ بِمَآ أَشۡرَكۡتُمُونِ مِن قَبۡلُۗ إِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
14:22.en: And Satan saith, when the matter hath been decided: Lo! Allah promised you a promise of truth; and I promised you, then failed you. And I had no power over you save that I called unto you and ye obeyed me. So blame not, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can ye help me, Lo! I disbelieved in that which ye before ascribed to me. Lo! for wrong-doers is a painful doom

40:18.ar: وَأَنذِرۡهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡأٓزِفَةِ إِذِ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ لَدَى ٱلۡحَنَاجِرِ كَٰظِمِينَۚ مَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ مِنۡ حَمِيمࣲ وَلَا شَفِيعࣲ يُطَاعُ
40:18.en: Warn them (O Muhammad) of the Day of the approaching (doom), when the hearts will be choking the throats, (when) there will be no friend for the wrong-doers, nor any intercessor who will be heard

40:19.ar: يَعۡلَمُ خَآئِنَةَ ٱلۡأَعۡيُنِ وَمَا تُخۡفِي ٱلصُّدُورُ
40:19.en: He knoweth the traitor of the eyes, and that which the bosoms hide

4:40.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظۡلِمُ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةࣲۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةࣰ يُضَٰعِفۡهَا وَيُؤۡتِ مِن لَّدُنۡهُ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:40.en: Lo! Allah wrongeth not even of the weight of an ant; and if there is a good deed, He will double it and will give (the doer) from His presence an immense reward

53:36.ar: أَمۡ لَمۡ يُنَبَّأۡ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ
53:36.en: Or hath he not had news of what is in the books of Moses

53:37.en: And Abraham who paid his debt

53:38.en: That no laden one shall bear another's load

16:25.ar: لِيَحۡمِلُوٓاْ أَوۡزَارَهُمۡ كَامِلَةࣰ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَمِنۡ أَوۡزَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُم بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمٍۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَزِرُونَ
16:25.en: That they may bear their burdens undiminished on the Day of Resurrection, with somewhat of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Ah! evil is that which they bear

6:160.ar: مَن جَآءَ بِٱلۡحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ عَشۡرُ أَمۡثَالِهَاۖ وَمَن جَآءَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ فَلَا يُجۡزَىٰٓ إِلَّا مِثۡلَهَا وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
6:160.en: Whoso bringeth a good deed will receive tenfold the like thereof, while whoso bringeth an ill-deed will be awarded but the like thereof; and they will not be wronged

25:70.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلࣰ ا صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَٰتࣲۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
25:70.en: Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

17:13.ar: وَكُلَّ إِنسَٰنٍ أَلۡزَمۡنَٰهُ طَٰٓئِرَهُۥ فِي عُنُقِهِۦۖ وَنُخۡرِجُ لَهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا يَلۡقَىٰهُ مَنشُورًا
17:13.en: And every man's augury have We fastened to his own neck, and We shall bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find wide open

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا
17:14.en: (And it will be said unto him): Read thy Book. Thy soul sufficeth as reckoner against thee this day

99:4.en: That day she will relate her chronicles

36:65.ar: ٱلۡيَوۡمَ نَخۡتِمُ عَلَىٰٓ أَفۡوَٰهِهِمۡ وَتُكَلِّمُنَآ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَتَشۡهَدُ أَرۡجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
36:65.en: This day We seal up their mouths, and their hands speak out to Us and their feet bear witness as to what they used to earn

41:20.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا مَا جَآءُوهَا شَهِدَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ سَمۡعُهُمۡ وَأَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ وَجُلُودُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
41:20.en: Till, when they reach it, their ears and their eyes and their skins testify against them as to what they used to do

41:21.ar: وَقَالُواْ لِجُلُودِهِمۡ لِمَ شَهِدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡنَاۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَنطَقَنَا ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنطَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ وَهُوَ خَلَقَكُمۡ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
41:21.en: And they say unto their skins: Why testify ye against us? They say: Allah hath given us speech Who giveth speech to all things, and Who created you at the first, and unto Whom ye are returned

19:95.en: And each one of them will come unto Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone

SUtszA1J9c8.speaker: adnan
SUtszA1J9c8.speaker_note: episode of his own Ramadan post-Fajr series on the stages of the Hereafter; single voice in his usual style
SUtszA1J9c8.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Rules of Judgement
SUtszA1J9c8.one_line: Shaytan's sermon, Allah's hundred mercies, the seven rules by which the reckoning runs, and the first two questions: blood and prayer.
SUtszA1J9c8.summary: With everyone across the bridge and the reckoning about to begin, he first describes Shaytan's sermon on that Day: the master con artist admits Allah's promise was true, says he had no power and only showed people something shiny, tells them to blame themselves and disowns them. Allah then releases the ninety-nine portions of mercy He kept back, so much that one must work hard to end up on the wrong side. He lays out seven rules of judgement: no injustice even an atom's weight, no one carries another's sin except the sins of those they misled, good deeds are multiplied tenfold, sins count only once and sincere repentance can flip them into good deeds, everything is documented in a book, witnesses testify from the earth, the angels and one's own limbs, and each person comes alone. Most chilling to him is that no one enters the Fire feeling wronged. The first questions concern blood and harm done to people, which only those people can forgive, then prayer, which carries every other deed. Since anyone closely examined is ruined, he urges each listener to find a deed great enough to outweigh the rest, as Musa's stand before Pharaoh outweighed his faults.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: everyone reaches the other side
outline.gist: He retraces the stages up to the bridge; everyone eventually reaches the other side, even those who fell, because this is where the reckoning begins.

outline.heading: Shaytan's sermon: Allah's promise was true
outline.gist: When all is decided Shaytan addresses humanity, admitting that Allah's promise was true and his own was empty.

outline.heading: The master con artist
outline.gist: Like the con artists in documentaries, he keeps hope going with 'next time', and his victims are ordinary people who were not critical enough.

outline.heading: Blame yourselves: Shaytan disowns his followers
outline.gist: He says he had no authority, he only showed them something attractive and they came, so they should blame themselves; he disowns all of it.

outline.heading: Warn them of the approaching Day
outline.gist: The hardest moment for those who let Shaytan lead them; Allah tells the Prophet to warn people of the Day when wrongdoers have no friend or intercessor.

outline.heading: Allah knows the stealthy glance
outline.gist: Allah knows every look of the eye and every hidden thought in the chest, and will judge with truth.

outline.heading: The hundred portions of mercy
outline.gist: Allah sent one part of mercy to the world, from which all compassion comes, and keeps ninety-nine for that Day; a narration says even Shaytan raises his head in hope.

outline.heading: Rule one: no injustice
outline.gist: Every hardship has already erased sins and mercy is spread wide; Allah wrongs no one even an atom's weight, so worry about yourself, not whether He will be fair to others.

outline.heading: Rule two: no one carries another's burden
outline.gist: Each person carries only their own sins, a principle found in the scriptures of Musa and Ibrahim.

outline.heading: The exception: sins of those you misled
outline.gist: Those who lead others into wrong carry their share too; a habit someone learned from you ripples back to you, as a share of every murder goes to the son of Adam who killed first.

outline.heading: Rule three: good deeds multiplied by ten
outline.gist: Every good deed is recorded tenfold at face value; Allah makes it very easy to succeed.

outline.heading: No one enters the Fire feeling wronged
outline.gist: Unlike convicts in this world who always feel hard done by, no one will enter Jahannam feeling unfairly treated, which he finds the most frightening part.

outline.heading: Rule four: a sin counts once, and repentance flips it
outline.gist: A sin is recorded only as itself, and sincere lifelong repentance turns past sins into good deeds; the man who sees this starts reminding Allah of sins he cannot find, and the Prophet laughed.

outline.heading: Rule five: everything is documented
outline.gist: The reckoning is written, not informal; each person reads a detailed book that includes intentions, feelings and thought processes.

outline.heading: Rule six: the earth testifies
outline.gist: The first witness is the earth, which saw everything done on its surface and will tell what its children did to one another.

outline.heading: Angels and limbs bear witness
outline.gist: The recording angels testify, and when people object their mouths are sealed and their hands and feet speak, until a person shouts at his own limbs.

outline.heading: Rule seven: you come alone
outline.gist: Each person comes by themselves; with the rules clear, people are called one by one by name to stand before Allah.

outline.heading: The questions are known: first, bloodshed
outline.gist: The exam questions are already leaked; the first matter judged between people is blood and any suffering you caused.

outline.heading: Come with clean hands
outline.gist: Allah may forgive His own rights, but harm done to people must be fixed now, because no one else can settle it; he wonders how those who bomb whole countries expect to be saved.

outline.heading: Prayer carries every other deed
outline.gist: The first deed asked about is salah, the vessel on which all other good deeds are carried; if you were not speaking to Allah throughout, He does not want the deeds.

outline.heading: Whoever is closely examined is ruined
outline.gist: If the reckoning becomes an argument over every day and every word, it is lost before it starts; no one can defend everything.

outline.heading: A deed that outweighs the rest: Musa
outline.gist: The Quran does not hold Musa's outbursts against him, while Yunus was tested for leaving his people, because Musa stood before a tyrant knowing he could be killed; find your own deed that earns that much credit.

outline.heading: This is the moment we are all heading to
outline.gist: Each person will be called, open their book and explain themselves, so bring something to show for your time on earth.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Prayer is the ongoing conversation with Allah that makes all other deeds acceptable.

themes.label: Courage and commitment
themes.note: Musa's stand before Pharaoh earned so much credit that his faults were set aside.

11:45.ar: وَنَادَىٰ نُوحࣱ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبۡنِي مِنۡ أَهۡلِي وَإِنَّ وَعۡدَكَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحۡكَمُ ٱلۡحَٰكِمِينَ
11:45.en: And Noah cried unto his Lord and said: My Lord! Lo! my son is of my household! Surely Thy promise is the truth and Thou are the Most Just of Judges

11:46.ar: قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيۡسَ مِنۡ أَهۡلِكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيۡرُ صَٰلِحࣲۖ فَلَا تَسۡـَٔلۡنِ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۖ إِنِّيٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
11:46.en: He said: O Noah! Lo! he is not of thy household; lo! he is of evil conduct, so ask not of Me that whereof thou hast no knowledge. I admonish thee lest thou be among the ignorant

21:63.ar: قَالَ بَلۡ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمۡ هَٰذَا فَسۡـَٔلُوهُمۡ إِن كَانُواْ يَنطِقُونَ
21:63.en: He said: But this, their chief hath done it. So question them, if they can speak

6:76.ar: فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلَّيۡلُ رَءَا كَوۡكَبࣰ اۖ قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَآ أُحِبُّ ٱلۡأٓفِلِينَ
6:76.en: When the night grew dark upon him he beheld a star. He said: This is my Lord. But when it set, he said: I love not things that set

6:77.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡقَمَرَ بَازِغࣰ ا قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَئِن لَّمۡ يَهۡدِنِي رَبِّي لَأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
6:77.en: And when he saw the moon uprising, he exclaimed: This is my Lord. But when it set, he said: Unless my Lord guide me, I surely shall become one of the folk who are astray

6:78.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلشَّمۡسَ بَازِغَةࣰ قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّي هَٰذَآ أَكۡبَرُۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَتۡ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنِّي بَرِيٓءࣱ مِّمَّا تُشۡرِكُونَ
6:78.en: And when he saw the sun uprising, he cried: This is my Lord! This is greater! And when it set he exclaimed: O my people! Lo! I am free from all that ye associate (with Him)

28:15.ar: وَدَخَلَ ٱلۡمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفۡلَةࣲ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيۡنِ يَقۡتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنۡ عَدُوِّهِۦۖ فَٱسۡتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِي مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِي مِنۡ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيۡهِۖ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنۡ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوࣱّ مُّضِلࣱّ مُّبِينࣱ‏
28:15.en: And he entered the city at a time of carelessness of its folk, and he found therein two men fighting, one of his own caste, and the other of his enemies; and he who was of his caste asked him for help against him who was of his enemies. So Moses struck him with his fist and killed him. He said: This is of the devil's doing. Lo! he is an enemy, a mere misleader

7:150.ar: وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ غَضۡبَٰنَ أَسِفࣰ ا قَالَ بِئۡسَمَا خَلَفۡتُمُونِي مِنۢ بَعۡدِيٓۖ أَعَجِلۡتُمۡ أَمۡرَ رَبِّكُمۡۖ وَأَلۡقَى ٱلۡأَلۡوَاحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأۡسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُۥٓ إِلَيۡهِۚ قَالَ ٱبۡنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱسۡتَضۡعَفُونِي وَكَادُواْ يَقۡتُلُونَنِي فَلَا تُشۡمِتۡ بِيَ ٱلۡأَعۡدَآءَ وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡنِي مَعَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
7:150.en: And when Moses returned unto his people, angry and grieved, he said: Evil is that (course) which ye took after I had left you. Would ye hasten on the judgment of your Lord? And he cast down the tablets, and he seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward him. He said: Son of my mother! Lo! the folk did judge me weak and almost killed me. Oh, make not mine enemies to triumph over me and place me not among the evil-doers

4:171.ar: يَٰٓأَهۡلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا تَغۡلُواْ فِي دِينِكُمۡ وَلَا تَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَقَّۚ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُۥٓ أَلۡقَىٰهَآ إِلَىٰ مَرۡيَمَ وَرُوحࣱ مِّنۡهُۖ فَـَٔامِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦۖ وَلَا تَقُولُواْ ثَلَٰثَةٌۚ ٱنتَهُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّكُمۡۚ إِنَّمَا ٱللَّهُ إِلَٰهࣱ وَٰحِدࣱۖ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥٓ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُۥ وَلَدࣱۘ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلࣰ ا
4:171.en: O People of the Scripture! Do not exaggerate in your religion nor utter aught concerning Allah save the truth. The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, was only a messenger of Allah, and His word which He conveyed unto Mary, and a spirit from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers, and say not "Three" - Cease! (it is) better for you! - Allah is only One Allah. Far is it removed from His Transcendent Majesty that He should have a son. His is all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. And Allah is sufficient as Defender

JJ96tJLuIeU.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Intercession to Begin Judgment (Day 19)
JJ96tJLuIeU.one_line: The great intercession: after years of waiting humanity goes from Adam to Isa, each declines, and the Prophet prostrates beneath the Throne until judgment begins.
JJ96tJLuIeU.summary: Built around a single narration in Bukhari and Muslim, the lesson picks up after the shade of the Throne: years pass with no word, and the waiting becomes so unbearable that billions of people come to want only one thing, for judgment to begin even if it leads to punishment. He notes that nothing is more stressful than waiting for a result, which pushes people to behave as they never would. Humanity goes to Adam, then Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Isa, and each says he can only care for himself, recalling a slip that was hardly a sin: Adam's lapse when new to life, Nuh's question about his son, Ibrahim's three statements that do not meet the definition of a lie, Musa's accidental killing and his anger at Harun, while Isa names nothing. The point is the sensitivity everyone will feel on that day once they see clearly who Allah is and who they are; no sin can then be justified, just as a child who broke something dares not speak to an angry father. He asks listeners to reach that realisation now rather than then. Finally the Prophet prostrates under the Throne, praises Allah as no one has before, is told to raise his head, and intercedes first for his people and then for judgment to begin.

outline.heading: Opening
Where we stand now
outline.gist: A recap of the stages so far, from the grave and the second blow to the collapse of the universe, the near sun, deeds taking physical form and the shade of the Throne. The lesson rests on one narration in Bukhari and Muslim.

outline.heading: Years of waiting with no word
outline.gist: Nothing happens; people stand for years, not hours or days, under unbearable stress.

outline.heading: Billions with one demand
outline.gist: Organising billions of people takes ages, yet eventually all of humanity says the same thing: this has to stop and whatever is next must begin.

outline.heading: Going to Adam
outline.gist: They go to the father of humanity and ask him to intercede for judgment to begin, even if they all end up in Jahannam.

outline.heading: Nothing is harder than waiting
outline.gist: Waiting for a result, even one you know is a failure, is the most anxiety-inducing experience; research shows people held waiting long enough do and say things they never would.

outline.heading: Adam: I can only care for myself
outline.gist: Adam declines and sends them to someone else.

outline.heading: A slip that was hardly a sin
outline.gist: Adam had just woken to life and did not yet understand desire, yet on that day everyone realises clearly whom they disobeyed and who they are.

outline.heading: No sin can be justified
outline.gist: Seeing Allah's greatness, no disobedience seems justifiable; like children who broke something and dare not speak to an angry father, no one dares address Him.

outline.heading: Realise it now, not then
outline.gist: Even those closest to Allah fear that day. We think our sins are no big deal, and he prays we grasp the gap between His status and ours before we reach the grave.

outline.heading: Nuh declines
outline.gist: Asked to intercede, Nuh recalls the supplication he used against his people and his question to Allah about his son.

outline.heading: Not sins, only less than perfect
outline.gist: Neither act was a sin, just not the ideal deed at that moment, yet Nuh dares not speak and sends them on.

outline.heading: Billions moving from prophet to prophet
outline.gist: All of humanity walks from one prophet to the next, and even those in the shade join, wanting the good that awaits them to begin.

outline.heading: Ibrahim the Khalil
outline.gist: They come to Ibrahim, Allah's most beloved companion, the highest status a human has reached, and he says it is a day of great wrath.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's three statements
outline.gist: The broken idols, the argument about the stars, and calling his wife his sister to save his life were not lies by definition, since a lie is self-serving deceit that harms others or escapes accountability. Yet he counts them, showing the sensitivity everyone feels that day.

outline.heading: Musa declines
outline.gist: The one Allah spoke to recalls accidentally killing a man while defending someone and his anger at Harun; these were mistakes, not sins.

outline.heading: Isa names no sin
outline.gist: The spirit and word of Allah mentions no mistake yet still declines, perhaps because people worshipped him. Then they come to the Prophet, who says this is his role.

outline.heading: Prostration beneath the Throne
outline.gist: The Prophet falls in prostration under the Throne and praises Allah with words no one has ever said before.

outline.heading: Raise your head
outline.gist: Allah tells him to raise his head, ask and intercede, the only person ever told this in prostration, a sign of Allah's full satisfaction with his life.

outline.heading: My people, then judgment for all
outline.gist: He first asks for his nation, three times, then intercedes for all humanity that the reckoning begin, and a first group of his people is admitted.

outline.heading: A gate as wide as hundreds of kilometres
outline.gist: The width between the gateposts of Jannah is like the distance between Makkah and a far city, and yet it will be packed that day.

29:16.ar: وَإِبۡرَٰهِيمَ إِذۡ قَالَ لِقَوۡمِهِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱتَّقُوهُۖ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
29:16.en: And Abraham! (Remember) when he said unto his folk: Serve Allah, and keep your duty unto Him; that is better for you if ye did but know

29:17.ar: إِنَّمَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡثَٰنࣰ ا وَتَخۡلُقُونَ إِفۡكًاۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ لَكُمۡ رِزۡقࣰ ا فَٱبۡتَغُواْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرِّزۡقَ وَٱعۡبُدُوهُ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لَهُۥٓۖ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
29:17.en: Ye serve instead of Allah only idols, and ye only invent a lie. Lo! those whom ye serve instead of Allah own no provision for you. So seek your provision from Allah, and serve Him, and give thanks unto Him, (for) unto Him ye will be brought back

6:76.ar: فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلَّيۡلُ رَءَا كَوۡكَبࣰ اۖ قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَآ أُحِبُّ ٱلۡأٓفِلِينَ

6:77.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡقَمَرَ بَازِغࣰ ا قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَئِن لَّمۡ يَهۡدِنِي رَبِّي لَأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ

2:260.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? 16:123.en: And afterward We inspired thee (Muhammad, saying): Follow the religion of Abraham, as one by nature upright. He was not of the idolaters

15:54.ar: قَالَ أَبَشَّرۡتُمُونِي عَلَىٰٓ أَن مَّسَّنِيَ ٱلۡكِبَرُ فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ

6:162.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحۡيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ

17:1.en: Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far distant place of worship the neighbourhood whereof We have blessed, that We might show him of Our tokens! Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Seer

24:11.en: Lo! they who spread the slander are a gang among you. Deem it not a bad thing for you; nay, it is good for you. Unto every man of them (will be paid) that which he hath earned of the sin; and as for him among them who had the greater share therein, his will be an awful doom

71:23.en: And they have said: Forsake not your gods. Forsake not Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr

39:3.ar: أَلَا لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡخَالِصُۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مَا نَعۡبُدُهُمۡ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ زُلۡفَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحۡكُمُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ فِي مَا هُمۡ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي مَنۡ هُوَ كَٰذِبࣱ كَفَّارࣱ‏
39:3.en: Surely pure religion is for Allah only. And those who choose protecting friends beside Him (say): We worship them only that they may bring us near unto Allah. Lo! Allah will judge between them concerning that wherein they differ. Lo! Allah guideth not him who is a liar, an ingrate

13:26.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُۚ وَفَرِحُواْ بِٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَٰعࣱ‏
13:26.en: Allah enlargeth livelihood for whom He will, and straiteneth (it for whom He will); and they rejoice in the life of the world, whereas the life of the world is but brief comfort as compared with the Hereafter

-ARmL6EJ8jk.title: Surah Al-Ankabut: Ibrahim's Call to Worship, Taqwa and Seeking Provision from Allah (29:16-17)
-ARmL6EJ8jk.one_line: Why the Prophet needed the stories of tested prophets, and Ibrahim's two-word summary of religion: worship Allah and be mindful of Him.
-ARmL6EJ8jk.summary: He recaps the surah's first section, then explains why the stories of tested prophets came to the Prophet late in Makkah: he had been tested in body, reputation, wealth, family and standing, and Madinah would bring even heavier burdens, so the Quran consoled and prepared him. No believer should expect to be spared what the prophets carried. Ibrahim's trial was having few followers and endless argument despite his overwhelming proof; the Quran calls him an ummah in himself, and today he is the most claimed figure on earth, with following him meaning keeping his creed. Ibrahim's call summarises the deen: worship, meaning a life of service to Allah, and taqwa, meaning constant self-accountability that keeps that service on track. 'That is better for you' means the benefit returns to us, in this world first; he sees this in hospital rooms with young patients facing terminal illness, where only these meanings hold a person steady. Idols are inventions without any basis, and people's capacity to invent religions, charms and superstitions is enormous, as Amr ibn Luhay's imported idols showed. Ibrahim cuts to the root: none of these own your provision, so seek it from Allah, worship and thank Him, for to Him you return.

outline.heading: Recap: no claim of faith without readiness for trial
outline.gist: Whoever claims faith must prepare for tests, and through patience reaches his goal on Judgment Day.

outline.heading: Pleasing people over Allah is hypocrisy
outline.gist: Testing is a law of the universe, light or heavy, short or long; yielding under it to please people or self is condemned.

outline.heading: Nuh's long trial; Ibrahim and Lut together
outline.gist: Nuh's test was duration; Lut, Ibrahim's relative and follower, left Iraq with him and Sarah.

outline.heading: The most tested are the prophets
outline.gist: The section passes through many prophets to show every one was tested.

outline.heading: The Prophet tested in body and reputation
outline.gist: After forty years of spotless character he was beaten and called a madman and sorcerer.

outline.heading: The boycott: when your family pays for your stand
outline.gist: Seeing relatives and followers suffer for your position is harder than suffering yourself, and holds many back from taking stands.

outline.heading: Loss of standing and family in Makkah
outline.gist: The grandson of the city's founders entered Makkah under another man's protection; his daughters were divorced, Khadijah and his uncle died.

outline.heading: Madinah would be harder still
outline.gist: Slander against his wife, the siege of the Trench, wounds at Uhud and the martyrdom of Hamzah lay ahead, so the surah prepared him.

outline.heading: Thirteen years against Nuh's 950
outline.gist: No prophet was tested in every area of life as he was, yet the Quran eases his burden with their stories.

outline.heading: Put yourself in his place
outline.gist: He had striven by tongue, wealth and patience in Makkah, but the harder striving of the battlefield was still to come.

outline.heading: Striving against the self versus combat
outline.gist: He follows the majority that combat is harder than self-discipline; still, the Prophet said not to wish to meet the enemy but to ask for well-being.

outline.heading: The burdens of leading a state
outline.gist: In Madinah he carried a people, an army and constant disputes; his white hairs appeared only there.

outline.heading: We are not exempt
outline.gist: If those Allah loves most were tested, we will be too; the stories run to verse forty.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's trial: few followers, endless argument
outline.gist: Recitation of the passage; unlike Nuh, Ibrahim was tested by having little following despite his overwhelming arguments.

outline.heading: Ibrahim the questioner
outline.gist: He questioned his father's statues, the star worshippers' gods and even asked Allah how He gives life.

outline.heading: "Ibrahim was an ummah": a man worth a thousand
outline.gist: Arabs praised a man as worth ten or a thousand; Umar sent Amr ibn al-'As four companions each counted as a thousand men.

outline.heading: A hundred camels and hardly one to ride
outline.gist: Few people can be relied on; the Prophet said Waraqah would be raised as an ummah on his own.

outline.heading: Few followers in life, the most followed today
outline.gist: Ibrahim did the work of a whole nation; now more people claim him than anyone, and following him means keeping his creed.

outline.heading: Ibrahim on the night of the Ascension
outline.gist: He leans on the Frequented House he resembled in building the Ka'bah, surrounded by children who die young, having himself waited long for sons.

outline.heading: "Tell your nation Paradise is open land"
outline.gist: Its plants are glorification, praise, tahlil and takbir: a deep message for those who reflect.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's repeated exiles
outline.gist: Thrown into fire in Babylon, threatened in Sham, endangered in Egypt, moving on to Palestine; he argued everywhere and few believed.

outline.heading: The land of his people and the Arab lineages
outline.gist: His people lived in a vast realm; the original Arabs descend from the peoples of Hud and Salih, the Arabised Arabs from Ismail.

outline.heading: Why Ismail's descendants multiplied
outline.gist: Arabs married daughters to men of standing and character, which is why Ismail's line spread; Islam later made character, not lineage, the criterion.

outline.heading: Worship is service; every Quranic word is precise
outline.gist: Different words mean different things; worship means devoting one's actions to serving Allah.

outline.heading: Taqwa: the accountability system that keeps worship on track
outline.gist: Without constant self-questioning before words and deeds, the self and Shaytan pull you off the path while you still claim to serve.

outline.heading: The whole deen in two words; "keep your tongue moist"
outline.gist: Ibrahim summarises religion as worship and taqwa; the Prophet told a man to keep his tongue moist with remembrance, which is taqwa.

outline.heading: "That is better for you"
outline.gist: The benefit of worship and taqwa returns to us, in this world first; many obey reluctantly without believing it is good for them.

outline.heading: What holds a person steady at a terminal diagnosis
outline.gist: In his work he sees young people with cancer; only those who absorbed these meanings withstand such trials without losing their faith.

outline.heading: Seven exiles and eighteen bereavements
outline.gist: Ibrahim was uprooted seven times; the Prophet lost eighteen close relatives yet woke each day smiling and returned to work.

outline.heading: "You worship only idols": wathan versus sanam
outline.gist: A sanam has a physical form; a wathan is any object of worship, including wealth and desire, chosen to escape commands, like the lenient mufti.

outline.heading: Ifk: smoke without fire
outline.gist: Ifk is a lie with no basis, as in the slander of Aisha; they 'create' it from nothing.

outline.heading: No prophet ever taught shirk
outline.gist: Neither Isa nor Musa nor the founders of other world traditions brought polytheism; people invented it.

outline.heading: The human talent for inventing religions
outline.gist: A person lies to himself, believes it, adds to it and spreads it; thousands have claimed prophethood, and their heirs grew rich.

outline.heading: Amr ibn Luhay imports idols
outline.gist: A trader saw idols for sale in Sham promising luck, sons and virility and brought them to Arabia; the Prophet saw him dragging his entrails in the Fire.

outline.heading: Charms and the evil eye today
outline.gist: Instead of blue beads and fear of people's eyes, recite morning and evening adhkar, the mu'awwidhat and Ayat al-Kursi, and do not flaunt blessings.

outline.heading: Righteous men turned into idols
outline.gist: The idols of Nuh's people were righteous men whose graves were glorified until they were worshipped as intercessors.

outline.heading: "They do not own any provision for you"
outline.gist: Ibrahim saw that the root is material: most intractable problems trace back to money and greed.

outline.heading: Seek provision from Allah; worship and thank Him
outline.gist: Idol cults ran on offerings; Allah alone expands and restricts provision, and Ash-Shakur rewards small deeds with Paradise.

outline.heading: Work hard, but humble yourself to no one; to Him you return
outline.gist: Strive for a living knowing provision comes only from Allah; it is hard to meet Him having worshipped or begged from others.

outline.heading: Outro

nlr7FguXcTM.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Outcome of Punishment
nlr7FguXcTM.one_line: The verdict of displeasure and what follows: the sinner offering his family as ransom, the pleas to Malik, and why nothing in life is worth it.
nlr7FguXcTM.summary: Picking up after the reckoning, he says there are only two outcomes and spends this night on the frightening one so that people take it seriously before he turns to Jannah. He imagines Allah saying to a servant that He is not pleased, and asks whether anything in an eighty-year life could be worth that moment. The Quran's scenes follow: no friend and no food but pus, the ultimate disgrace, the condemned man who would hand over his children, spouse, siblings and all humanity to be spared, the plea to Malik to end their existence, the request for water from the people of Jannah, and the promise to behave perfectly if sent back, answered with 'did We not give you a life long enough?'. Narrations add that Jibril found the Fire surrounded by desires and that the most comfortable person in the world forgets every good day after one dip in it. He argues that people this weak have no grounds for arrogance, and that the existence of Hell is a warning to act on, not information to file away. Since people enter it in groups, look at who you spend your time with.

outline.heading: Opening
Hoping Allah overlooks the rest
outline.gist: After the critical moment of judgement, all we can do is pray and prepare something for which Allah looks past every other detail instead of questioning each line of the book.

outline.heading: Only two outcomes: the verdict
outline.gist: Like a court with Allah as judge and all the witnesses, the reckoning ends in a verdict, and there are essentially two outcomes.

outline.heading: "My servant, I am not pleased with you"
outline.gist: Some will be told that Allah does not accept what they did and be taken to punishment.

outline.heading: Is anything worth that moment?
outline.gist: Whatever joy or hardship filled a long life, none of it matters when those words are said; ask whether the way you live now is worth hearing them.

outline.heading: No friend and no food
outline.gist: The verdict is final; on that day no one stands up for this person or befriends them, and their only food is the discharge of the wounds.

outline.heading: The ultimate disgrace
outline.gist: He leaves the full description to the Quran, which calls entry into Jahannam total disgrace for whoever opposes Allah.

outline.heading: They see their families
outline.gist: The condemned are shown their brothers, spouses, children and parents, and eyes meet.

outline.heading: Take my children, just spare me
outline.gist: The one who would have thrown himself before a bus for his children now offers them, his spouse, his siblings and everyone on earth as ransom.

outline.heading: Everyone but the parents; 'is there more?'
outline.gist: They leave out their parents because they finally learned what displeases Allah, too late; Jahannam is asked whether it is full and asks for more.

outline.heading: The plea to Malik
outline.gist: The people of the Fire beg its keeper to ask Allah to end their existence altogether and are told they will remain.

outline.heading: If you knew what I know
outline.gist: The Prophet said people would laugh little and weep much if they saw what he saw; he begins the narration of Jibril being sent to look at Jahannam.

outline.heading: Jahannam surrounded by desires
outline.gist: Jibril first thought no one would enter it, but once it was surrounded by cheap, instant pleasures he feared no one would escape it.

outline.heading: Pour us some water / send us back
outline.gist: The people of the Fire ask those in Jannah for any water or food and are refused, then promise to make no mistakes if returned.

outline.heading: Did We not give you a life long enough?
outline.gist: They are answered that they had time, chances and a warner who explained everything.

outline.heading: Small creatures who refused the path
outline.gist: We are tiny beings on a speck orbiting an old sun, given clear rules and a clear outcome; those too arrogant to follow them face what awaits.

outline.heading: Beds and coverings of fire
outline.gist: Their bed is of Jahannam with fire above them; every surah of the last part of the Quran describes some piece of it.

outline.heading: Shade of black smoke for those who lived in luxury
outline.gist: Scorching wind, boiling water and a shade that is neither cool nor kind await those who once lived in comfort.

outline.heading: Allah means business
outline.gist: Hearing this should make people take the warning seriously; if there were only Jannah or nothing, people would lack the motive to choose right.

outline.heading: What grounds do we have for arrogance?
outline.gist: We cannot provide for ourselves for most of our early lives, so our confidence in disobeying makes no sense; a pinhole opened in Jahannam would burn everything.

outline.heading: The sight of its guardian
outline.gist: Had people seen the guardian of Jahannam they would not sleep or even bury their dead; he urges them to read the Quran's descriptions themselves.

outline.heading: What will you do with this information?
outline.gist: Hell is a real possible outcome with a million ways to end up there, so it has to change decisions, not be ignored.

outline.heading: Did no warner come to you?
outline.gist: As each group is thrown in, the keepers ask whether no one warned them; they admit they were warned and called it a lie, and had they thought they would not be there.

outline.heading: Look at who you walk with
outline.gist: People are driven in groups, so look left and right at who you spend your time with, because that is the group you will be with.

outline.heading: One dip erases a lifetime of comfort
outline.gist: No wealth, health, status or power is worth that moment; the most comfortable person dipped once in the Fire will say he never saw a good day.

BbPzXCYCJ7k.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The First Blow of the Horn (Day 12)
BbPzXCYCJ7k.one_line: The first blow of the horn ends all life, leaving Allah alone, and he draws from it a call to treat life itself as the greatest gift.
BbPzXCYCJ7k.summary: He closes the stage of the grave, noting that a hard start there can turn to ease as sins are expiated, and explains that the series will skip the signs of the Hour, which the Quran barely mentions, to focus on what it describes on almost every page. He warns that the order of events is not fully specified, and that despite popular talk we are far from the end of time. He then describes the first blow of the horn: a single blast that strikes everyone mid-dispute and mid-task, leaving no time to make amends, illustrated by narrations of people who never finish a sale, a drink or a mouthful. The angel of death takes the life of Israfil and then his own, and Allah alone remains, calling out for the kings and tyrants of the earth while the Prophet's minbar shook. From this he builds his main reflection: we are guests on existence who never existed before and soon will not again, so we should stop acting entitled to life, notice its beauty, and use it to know Allah. Life itself is the ultimate blessing, and Islam the second.

outline.heading: Opening
Closing the stage of the grave
outline.gist: Some have a hard beginning in the grave that Allah turns to ease as their sins are forgiven; the reverse does not happen to those who start well.

outline.heading: Why the series skips the signs of the Hour
outline.gist: Muslims spend much time on the minor and major signs, which the Quran barely mentions, while it describes the events of the hereafter on almost every page; that is what deserves study.

outline.heading: The order of events is not fixed
outline.gist: Scholars present slightly different sequences because the Quran does not spell it out; he will give the most rational order he can.

outline.heading: We are far from the end of time
outline.gist: The end comes when hardly anyone believes and the masjids are empty, which is not yet the case; almost all of us will die before it, and only Allah knows its timing.

outline.heading: The first blow strikes everyone
outline.gist: When the horn is first blown, everyone in the heavens and earth falls dead except whom Allah wills, and a second blow follows later.

outline.heading: One blast with no time to make amends
outline.gist: People are seized while arguing over worldly matters, unable to leave a will or return to their families, the first quake followed by the second.

outline.heading: How the companions coped with the horn
outline.gist: The Prophet's words about the angel ready to blow distressed the companions, and he told them to say that Allah is sufficient and to rely on Him. The Quran gives the Day over twenty-five names, each showing one aspect.

outline.heading: The first to hear the horn
outline.gist: A man mending a water trough looks up, hears the sound and collapses, and then the rest of humanity follows.

outline.heading: Cut off mid-task
outline.gist: The Hour comes while two men have spread out a garment to trade, a man carries milk home, another fixes a basin and another lifts food to his mouth; none of them finish.

outline.heading: The death of Israfil and the angel of death
outline.gist: Allah tells the angel of death to take the life of the one who blew the horn, then to take his own life. A span of forty passes in which nothing exists.

outline.heading: Guests on existence
outline.gist: We contributed nothing to this extraordinary journey and barely understand it, yet we rush from one hurdle to the next without noticing it. Stop treating life as a right you are owed and you will live it differently.

outline.heading: Where are the kings of the earth?
outline.gist: With the heavens and earth in His hand, Allah calls out by His names, the King, the Compeller, the Creator, asking where the tyrants and kings are. The minbar shook under the Prophet as he described it.

outline.heading: We never existed before
outline.gist: Knowing we were nothing and will be nothing again brings relief, and should make us live respectfully of that moment. We cling to life because we forget this, and most people do not respect the fact that they are alive.

outline.heading: Life is the ultimate blessing
outline.gist: Allah gave us senses and opportunities so we would know Him and leave the world grateful; life itself is the greatest blessing and Islam the second.

outline.heading: Silence when only Allah remains
outline.gist: No more fighting or shouting: one wave silences everyone at once. What exists when time and space are removed is beyond our comprehension.

outline.heading: Israfil revived for the second blow
outline.gist: Allah always was and always will be, while we enjoy a few laps around the sun. He gives life back to the angel of the horn to blow again.

GcGPvw9pJQA.speaker_note: final episode of his own Ramadan post-Fajr series on the stages of the Hereafter; single voice in his usual style
GcGPvw9pJQA.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Outcome of Reward
GcGPvw9pJQA.one_line: The series closes with the people of the heights, the moment Allah says 'I have accepted you', and what Jannah truly holds: knowledge, peace and seeing Allah.
GcGPvw9pJQA.summary: Closing the series, he recaps the journey from death to judgement, then notes the people of the heights between Jannah and the Fire, whom he reads as those who never cared enough to commit either way and are left forgotten as they lived. He then walks through a reckoning that goes well: deeds accepted, few questions, and yet no real safety until both feet are inside Jannah, since unpaid rights to people can still pull one back. The golden words, 'My servant, I have accepted you', make every past pain irrelevant, like graduation. He describes Jannah less through its food and pleasures than through what the Quran emphasises: radiant faces, hearts united as one, no hurtful speech, new senses beyond imagination, direct access to knowledge that ends all anxiety, and above all seeing Allah. Praise there flows only from those who enjoyed it here. He recounts the last person to enter Jannah, the weekly gathering with Allah and His granting of His lasting pleasure, then the slaughter of death and the final intercession. He ends by urging people not to trade this destiny for small, forgettable pleasures and to read the Quran to know exactly what they are aiming for.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap of the whole journey
outline.gist: From accepting mortality and death through the grave, the horn, the resurrection, the books, the scales, the parade of Jahannam and the rules of judgement, to the bad outcome described last time.

outline.heading: The people of the heights: those who didn't care
outline.gist: Scholars differ on who stand between Jannah and the Fire; he reads them as people who were never committed either way, left forgotten just as they lived.

outline.heading: A reckoning that goes smoothly
outline.gist: Your book is in your right hand, the scales look reasonable, and much of what you read has been forgiven through good deeds and blessed nights.

outline.heading: Deeds that are accepted
outline.gist: A good deed is only worth something if accepted; if Allah broke each down by sincerity and focus few would stand, so you hope for few questions and a quick verdict.

outline.heading: Not safe until both feet are in
outline.gist: There is no rest until you are fully inside Jannah, because an outstanding right owed to someone can still pull you back.

outline.heading: "My servant, I have accepted you"
outline.gist: The most valuable words you will ever hear invite you among His servants into His Jannah, and every pain, grudge and unresolved problem stops mattering.

outline.heading: Like graduation day
outline.gist: Just as the hard course is forgotten once you graduate, all of life is condensed into that verdict, the moment of true celebration.

outline.heading: The Prophet opens the door; hearts become one
outline.gist: The Prophet is the first to knock and the keeper was told to open for no one before him; inside, people's hearts are like one heart, something that never exists in this world.

outline.heading: Praise there flows from love here
outline.gist: People in Jannah glorify Allah because they love to; if you do not enjoy praising Him now, it will not suddenly become who you are there.

outline.heading: No sorrow, fear, disease or pain
outline.gist: Hunger, thirst, agony and every painful emotion are simply removed.

outline.heading: Seeing Jannah through radiant faces
outline.gist: The Quran describes the people more than the place: you see its bliss through the brightness and calm in their faces.

outline.heading: Nothing hurtful is heard; no soul knows what awaits
outline.gist: No cursing or idle talk reaches them, only what they want to hear, and no one knows what joy has been hidden for them.

outline.heading: What no eye has seen: new senses
outline.gist: Try to imagine a new sense and you cannot; Jannah brings senses beyond ours, so it is far more than food, drink and relationships.

outline.heading: Infinite knowledge ends all anxiety
outline.gist: Everything about past, future and creation is explained, and since anxiety comes from the unknown, that clarity brings complete peace.

outline.heading: Life begins there; this is preparation
outline.gist: Unimaginable creations and realities await, and this world is the preparation period in which to get your thoughts straight and know where you are going.

outline.heading: The last person to enter Jannah
outline.gist: He keeps asking for one more tree, promising it is his last request, until he is let in, and is offered the dominion of the greatest king on earth.

outline.heading: Ten times the world, and the highest ranks
outline.gist: The least is given many times the world and needs a thousand years to see it; for the highest, Allah planted their honour with His own hand and sealed it.

outline.heading: Seeing Allah
outline.gist: The people of the highest ranks care for nothing in Jannah as much as their next meeting with Allah; looking at Him is the whole point.

outline.heading: The weekly gathering and Allah's lasting pleasure
outline.gist: Every week they gather, Allah addresses them and they return more beautiful; He asks if they are pleased and grants His pleasure, never to be displeased with them again.

outline.heading: All praise to Allah; death slaughtered; the last intercession
outline.gist: Judgement closes with praise of the Lord of the worlds, death is brought and slaughtered, and after the righteous, angels and prophets intercede, the Most Merciful brings out more.

outline.heading: Don't trade your destiny for small pleasures
outline.gist: Do not let a passing emotion, whim or momentary high take you away from what you were made for; fulfil that destiny yourself, and read the Quran to know your target.

outline.heading: Outro

57:12.ar: يَوۡمَ تَرَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَسۡعَىٰ نُورُهُم بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَبِأَيۡمَٰنِهِمۖ بُشۡرَىٰكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ جَنَّٰتࣱ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
57:12.en: On the day when thou (Muhammad) wilt see the believers, men and women, their light shining forth before them and on their right hands, (and wilt hear it said unto them): Glad news for you this day: Gardens underneath which rivers flow, wherein ye are immortal. That is the supreme triumph

57:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتُ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱنظُرُونَا نَقۡتَبِسۡ مِن نُّورِكُمۡ قِيلَ ٱرۡجِعُواْ وَرَآءَكُمۡ فَٱلۡتَمِسُواْ نُورࣰ اۖ فَضُرِبَ بَيۡنَهُم بِسُورࣲ لَّهُۥ بَابُۢ بَاطِنُهُۥ فِيهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةُ وَظَٰهِرُهُۥ مِن قِبَلِهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُ
57:13.en: On the day when the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women will say unto those who believe: Look on us that we may borrow from your light! it will be said: Go back and seek for light! Then there will separate them a wall wherein is a gate, the inner side whereof containeth mercy, while the outer side thereof is toward the doom

57:14.ar: يُنَادُونَهُمۡ أَلَمۡ نَكُن مَّعَكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِنَّكُمۡ فَتَنتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَتَرَبَّصۡتُمۡ وَٱرۡتَبۡتُمۡ وَغَرَّتۡكُمُ ٱلۡأَمَانِيُّ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ وَغَرَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡغَرُورُ
57:14.en: They will cry unto them (saying): Were we not with you? They will say: Yea, verily; but ye tempted one another, and hesitated, and doubted, and vain desires beguiled you till the ordinance of Allah came to pass; and the deceiver deceived you concerning Allah

57:15.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ لَا يُؤۡخَذُ مِنكُمۡ فِدۡيَةࣱ وَلَا مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۚ مَأۡوَىٰكُمُ ٱلنَّارُۖ هِيَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
57:15.en: So this day no ransom can be taken from you nor from those who disbelieved. Your home is the Fire; that is your patron, and a hapless journey's end

57:16.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ يَأۡنِ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَن تَخۡشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمۡ لِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا نَزَلَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَطَالَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَمَدُ فَقَسَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡۖ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
57:16.en: Is not the time ripe for the hearts of those who believe to submit to Allah's reminder and to the truth which is revealed, that they become not as those who received the scripture of old but the term was prolonged for them and so their hearts were hardened, and many of them are evil-livers

URfFMO9q8KY.speaker: adnan
URfFMO9q8KY.speaker_note: episode of his own Ramadan post-Fajr series on the stages of the Hereafter; single voice in his usual style
URfFMO9q8KY.title: Stages of the Hereafter: The Basin and the Bridge (Sirat)
URfFMO9q8KY.one_line: The Prophet's basin and those driven away from it for changing his way, then the bridge over Jahannam crossed by the light of one's deeds.
URfFMO9q8KY.summary: After recapping the stages up to the setting of the scales, he describes the Prophet's basin: vast, brighter than silver, more fragrant than musk, and one drink ends thirst forever. The Prophet waits there for his followers and recognises them by the glow of wudu, yet some are pulled away at the last moment because they did not walk his path and changed what he taught. He insists the deen is simple, rituals and service, and that whoever complicates or bends it to an agenda risks being snatched away just before reaching it. The Prophet's appointment at the basin should shape how we use our time, as a story about Ibn al-Jawzi refusing idle chatter shows. He then describes the bridge stretched over Jahannam, thin as a blade and lined with hooks, crossed at speeds ranging from lightning to crawling, and ties it to the straight path we ask for in every prayer: as you walk it here, you will walk it there. In the darkness only the believers' light lets them cross, while hypocrites are told to go back for it. He ends with the verse asking whether the time has come for hearts to soften, urging people to gather their light now.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: from the graves to the scales
outline.gist: He retraces the stages so far up to the setting of the scales and the value system they make clear, then introduces the basin.

outline.heading: The Prophet's basin
outline.gist: It takes a month to cross, is brighter than silver and more fragrant than musk, and whoever drinks from it is changed and never thirsts again.

outline.heading: The Prophet keeps a place for his ummah
outline.gist: He pushes others away from the basin as a man drives strangers' camels from his own trough, so that his followers drink first.

outline.heading: Recognised by the glow of wudu
outline.gist: Followers he never met are known by light shining from the places washed in wudu, earned on every cold Fajr when they could have stayed in bed.

outline.heading: Driven away: you don't know what they did after you
outline.gist: He fills cups for people he recognises, but they are pulled away because they did not honour his legacy, his ethics or his way of life and led others astray.

outline.heading: The text is protected, the values are not
outline.gist: The Quran cannot be altered as earlier scriptures were, but people can twist its values, chase secondary issues and push agenda-driven narratives that bury its selflessness and service.

outline.heading: The deen is simple
outline.gist: Islam is not complicated: perform your rituals and serve people; anyone who made it complicated for you did you a disservice.

outline.heading: Snatched away an arm's length from it
outline.gist: Some are pulled away a moment before drinking, just as they were handed Jannah in the form of the Quran and chose to change, pick and leave parts of what he taught.

outline.heading: The appointment at the basin
outline.gist: The Prophet put off worldly socialising because his meeting place with his followers is the basin; he asks them to arrive there having done things properly.

outline.heading: Ibn al-Jawzi has no time for idle talk
outline.gist: Asked by a childhood friend to sit and chat, Ibn al-Jawzi replied that he would if the friend could stop the sun, showing how seriously the early scholars took time.

outline.heading: The bridge laid over Jahannam
outline.gist: Scholars differ on the exact timing, but he holds that Jahannam now becomes visible to everyone as a vast pit that must be crossed to reach the place of reckoning.

outline.heading: Thin as a blade and lined with hooks
outline.gist: The bridge is as fine as a sword's edge with swinging hooks along it, like the thorns of a plant the companions knew.

outline.heading: No one knows anyone at three moments
outline.gist: Even the prophets only plead for safety; he returns to Aisha's question and the three moments when nobody cares for anyone else: the flying books, the scales and the crossing of the bridge.

outline.heading: Crossing at different speeds
outline.gist: Some cross like lightning or the blink of an eye, others like a shooting star or a galloping horse, some stumble across and some fall.

outline.heading: As you walk the path here, you walk it there
outline.gist: It is called the sirat for a reason: whoever walks the straight path they ask for in every prayer with focus and without hesitation will cross it the same way.

outline.heading: Light in the pitch dark
outline.gist: Some crawl, caught by hook after hook, and fall just before the end; the crossing is in total darkness and believers glow with their own light, which is the only way to see.

outline.heading: Good news for the believers, the hypocrites ask for light
outline.gist: Believers are given the glad tidings of Jannah, while hypocrites beg them to wait so they can borrow their light.

outline.heading: Go back and seek light: the wall with a door
outline.gist: The hypocrites are told to look behind them for light, meaning back in time to the world; a wall rises with mercy on one side and punishment on the other.

outline.heading: Were we not with you?
outline.gist: They protest that they were Muslims alongside the believers and are told they deceived themselves with false hope and wishful thinking, and no ransom is accepted.

outline.heading: Has the time not come for hearts to soften?
outline.gist: The very next verse asks believers whether it is not time for their hearts to humble themselves; he asks what we are waiting for to gather our light.

outline.heading: No one dares look down
outline.gist: On the bridge each person worries only about themselves and looks straight ahead, not daring to see what lies below.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Describes the Prophet's basin and the bridge over Jahannam in detail.

themes.label: Love: of Allah, the Prophet, and one another
themes.note: The Prophet's eagerness to meet his followers, keep their place and recognise them at the basin.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Those driven from the basin are those who changed his teaching, chose the parts they liked and did not walk his path.

themes.label: Priorities in the deen: fundamentals before details
themes.note: The deen is simple, rituals and service; obsessing over secondary issues and complicating it distorts it.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: The Prophet and scholars like Ibn al-Jawzi guarded their time because of the meeting awaiting them.

themes.label: Istiqamah: incorruptibility, steadfastness, moral integrity
themes.note: How steadily you walk the straight path in life decides how you cross the bridge.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: Hypocrites who stood with the believers in the world are left without light and cut off by the wall.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: The call for hearts to soften toward Allah now, before that day.

hadith.gist: The Prophet's basin is a month's journey across, whiter than silver, more fragrant than musk, and whoever drinks from it never thirsts again
The Prophet will push people from his basin as a man drives other people's camels from his trough
His ummah will be recognised by the shining marks of wudu
People will be driven away from the basin and he will be told: you do not know what they did after you
The bridge is finer than a sword's edge with hooks like the thorns of the sa'dan plant
Aisha asked whether people remember their loved ones; no one remembers anyone at the books, the scales and the bridge
People cross the bridge according to their deeds: like lightning, the blink of an eye, wind, horses, some crawling, some falling

maxims: Islam is dead simple: perform your rituals and serve people
However you walk the sirat here, you will walk it there
Your light is behind you: go back and get it

stories.who: Ibn al-Jawzi and his childhood friend
stories.point: Invited to idle chat, he said stop the sun first; the early scholars treated time as too precious to waste.

takeaways: Guard Fajr and wudu, the marks by which the Prophet will recognise you.
Follow the Prophet's teaching whole, without picking parts or twisting it to suit an agenda.
Keep the deen simple: do the rituals and serve people.
Walk the straight path steadily now, since that is how you will cross the bridge.
Gather your light through deeds today; do not wait for your heart to soften.
